name: OpenMW Dynamic Animations
author: taitechnic
description: UPDATE: Limit the speed of footstep sounds in First Person. Adds a bit of visual variance to NPC's, by customizing their walk style and adding some extra idle animations.
usage_notes:
[size=6][u][b][color=#ff7700][center]Dynamic Animations[/center][/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=5]The key features :[/size]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]Variable walk speed[/b][/size][/color]
[size=3]Applies a speed cap to wandering NPC's. Stops the unarmoured ones from rushing around like hyperactive ants, as they tend to do in the normal game. The smaller their wander radius is, the lower the speed cap.[/size]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]Modified walk animations[/b][/size][/color]
[size=3]Guards are given a distinct walking style. Slower walking NPC's have a slightly different animation from faster walking ones. These changes only apply to wandering NPC's.[/size]

[b][color=#00ffff][size=4]Modified Argonian body shape proportions[/size][/color][/b]
[size=3]Included is a version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/50101]Argonian Anatomy[/url], modified to fix the "head popping" issue that occurs when used with OpenMW. Thanks to the original authors of that mod.[/size]

[b][color=#00ffff][size=4]Custom walk animation for the Player[/size][/color][/b]
[size=3]Select a unique walk animation for the player. This feature is fully working, but is currently of limited use. Apart from [b]Dirnae's[/b] walk animation (most people will be using this already), there are no other alternative walk animations that have been made for Morrowind (that are publicly available). The vanilla Morrowind walk and Dirnae's walk are included as options, if anybody wants to test this feature out in-game.[/size]


[u][b][size=4]Installation and Requirements[/size][/b][/u]

[size=3]Requires OpenMW 0.49 or better. Files should be installed in the same way as other OpenMW lua script mods, and then enable "Dynamic Animations.omwscripts" in the game launcher.

Check the following options are enabled in the game launcher settings :

[list]
[*][color=#ff7700][b][u]Visuals --> Use additional animation sources[/u][/b][/color]
[*][color=#ff7700][b][u]Visuals --> Smooth Animation Transitions[/u][/b][/color]
[*][color=#ff7700][b][u]Gameplay --> Racial variation in speed fix[/u][/b][/color] : Optional, but recommended to avoid inconsistent walking speed caps for NPC's.
[/list]
[/size]
[b][u][size=5]Compatibility with other mods[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]There is a settings page provided to disable unwanted features.[/size]

[color=#ff7700][size=4][b][u]Dynamic Actors[/u][/b][/size][/color][size=3] : The files from this mod need to be overridden by the ones from Dynamic Animations. This can be done in the game launcher by setting the data directory for Dynamic Animations to load after Dynamic Actors.[/size]

[b][color=#ff7700][size=4][u]Argonian Anatomy[/u][/size][/color][/b][size=3] : Shouldn't be needed if Dynamic Animations is installed.[/size]

[b][size=4]Other mods[/size][/b][size=3] : No NPC stats are modified by this mod, and any NPC not using a wander package (in combat, travelling etc.) will be ignored.[/size]


[b][u][size=5]Credits :[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]Male and Beast walk animations based on original work by Dirnae.[/size]

[size=3]Female noble walk animation based on original work by Axel.[/size]

[size=3]Argonian Anatomy animation made by C3pa / Qwerty / HedgeHog12[/size]

name: Zerkish ModUtils (OpenMW)
author: Zerkish
description: Utility Lua Library, does nothing on its own.
usage_notes:
[center][size=6][b][color=#f6b26b]Zerkish ModUtils[/color]
[/b][/size][/center]
[size=4][b][color=#f6b26b]For Users[/color]

[/b][/size][size=2]ZModUtils is a utility library for [b]OpenMW[/b]/Lua that contains some utility functions for common calculations like SpellSchools, Armor Ratings as well as a small UI library with functions for scrollbars, buttons, clickable text elements etc.

[b][color=#ffff00]There's no reason to download this unless you're using a mod that depends on it.[/color][/b][/size]

[color=#f6b26b][size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size][/color]

[size=2]Steps:

[/size][list=1]
[*][size=2]Download the main file from the File Page[/size]
[*][size=2]Unzip wherever you keep your mods[/size]
[*][size=2]Open the OpenMW launcher[/size]
[*][size=2]In the [i]Data Files[/i] tab: Add the [b]ZModUtils folder[/b] from the archive to your data paths in the OpenMW launcher, [b]before [/b]any mod that requires it.[/size]
[*][size=2]In the [i]Content Files[/i] tab: Add ZModUtils.omwscripts, put it before any mod that depends on it in the list.[/size]
[*][size=2]Done![/size]
[/list]

[color=#f6b26b][size=3][b]Other Mods by Me[/b][/size][/color]

[size=2]Other mods by me, some of them require ZModUtils, some don't, check their individual pages.

[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56583]Zerkish Hotkeys Improved[/url]
[*]﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56718]Zerkish AutoSave[/url]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56797]Zerkish SkillTracker[/url]﻿

[/list][/size][b][color=#f6b26b][size=3]
[/size][/color][/b][color=#f6b26b]
[b][size=4]For Mod Developers[/size][/b][/color]

[size=2]You are free to use ZModUtils as a dependency, but [i]be [b]warned[/b][/i] it is not a stable API (as in I may update it and break your mods), and it's not well documented. I mainly made this to share code between my own mods. It's likely better to look at the code and "[i]borrow" [/i]parts that you need.

If you have questions you can contact me here on Nexus or the OpenMW discord.[/size]

name: Zerkish AutoSave (For OpenMW)
author: Zerkish
description: Simple Reliable AutoSaves
usage_notes:
[center][b][color=#f6b26b][size=6]Zerkish AutoSave[/size][/color][/b][/center]

[center][color=#93c47d][size=3][b]Please remember to endorse the mod if you enjoy it![/b][/size][/color][/center]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/CBAElYb.png[/img][/center]﻿
[color=#ffd966][center][i][u][size=4]Beta[/size][/u][/i]
[i][size=2]Zerkish AutoSave is currently in "beta", which means that most of the core functionality is in place but it is not well tested yet.
[/size][i][size=2]This means use at your own risk, and save frequently.[/size]
[/i]
[size=2]Bug reports are encouraged!
Try to include as much information as possible, and your openmw.log file.[/size][/i][/center][/color]


[color=#f6b26b][size=4][b]Information[/b][/size][/color]

Zerkish AutoSave is a [b]simple[/b] autosave mod for OpenMW.
The goal is to provide a mod that [b]guarantees [/b]saves are made close to the timespan provided by the player. 

[b][color=#f1c232][size=2]!Important! Do [i]not [/i]label your manual saves 'ZSave###' or they will be overwritten/deleted by the mod.[/size][/color][/b]

[i][size=2]Due to the critical nature of a save mod, I suggest making manual saves, and backups.[/size][/i]

[b][color=#f6b26b][size=4]Features[/size][/color][/b]

[list]
[*]Maintain a configurable number of save slots (Default 5)
[*]Optional AutoSave on a time interval, tracked by [i][b]real-time.[/b] [/i]This means time spent in menus [i]does [/i]count toward the autosave timer. (Default 15 minutes)
[*]Optional AutoSave on entering a new area/cell, with a delay configurable in settings. Going from exterior->exterior is [b]not [/b]considered a new area. (Default 30 seconds)
[*][b]AutoSave Verification[/b]: After saving, the mod will keep checking to ensure the save was actually made, and if not retry again asap.
[/list]

author: rot

Did you think Kwama foragers were meant to attack by wiggling at you? No, they spit. But most creature particle effects weren't displayed for technical reasons. Some of the more noticeable fixes are for bodies that disappear on death, like Dremora or Ghosts, or steam effects for Dwemer constructs.

Fixes[/center][/b]

﻿﻿-- STEAM: ﻿﻿Centurion Archer, Centurion Sphere, Steam Centurion, Yagrum Bagarn
-- ATTACK EFFECTS: Flame Atronach, Frost Atronach, Kwama Forager

name: No-Frills Open Vivec
author: Atrayonis
description: Opens up Vivec and (optionally) moves the Foreign Quarter canton a bit.
usage_notes:
[size=4][size=5]W[/size]HAT DOES THIS MOD DO?[/size]

Yet another Open Vivec mod.
 
It is available in two basic flavours in a BAIN archive:

[i][b]No-Frills Open Vivec (Paper Map Placement)[/b][/i]

This version makes no changes other than opening Vivec's cantons and placing the Foreign Quarter into a symmetrical position more akin to the paper map that shipped with Morrowind. No big changes otherwise, no additional lights, signposts, or similar.

[b][i]No-Frills Open Vivec (Vanilla Placement)[/i][/b]

Exact same thing, except the cantons are not moved.

[size=4][size=4][size=5]I[/size]SN'T IT TERRIBLY INCOMPATIBLE WITH EVERYTHING?[/size][/size]

As with every other Open Vivec mod, incompatibilities exist with other mods that change the Plaza cells. The paper map version moreso because the Foreign Quarter canton has been moved.
    
Patches available for [b]both[/b] versions:
[list][*]Uvirith's Legacy (the Vivec fast travel location is in the Telvanni plaza)
[*]Main Quest Enhancers (Imperial Intolerance, the other parts require no patch)
[/list]Patches available for the [b]Vanilla Placement[/b] version:
[list][*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48683]Stav's Mages Guilds Overhaul[/url]﻿ (requires the ESM version)
[/list]   
[size=4][size=5]A[/size]NY FUTURE PLANS?[/size]

More patches.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48256]Rethinking Vivec[/url] is what this mod was a stepping stone for so there should not be any future changes other than patches.

[size=4][size=5]W[/size]HO IS TO BLAME FOR THIS MESS?[/size]

The Elder Scrolls, Morrowind, etc. are property of Bethesda Softworks.

As usual, I am standing on the shoulder of giants.

name: Arrive Whenever - Start Time and Timescale for OpenMW
author: Leaposter
description: Configurable arrival time and timescale when starting a new game.
usage_notes:
[b]Description:[/b]
You've heard of "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51567]Arrive At Night[/url]" and "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59179]Arrive Before Dawn[/url]", now get ready for "[b]Arrive Whenever[/b]"!
This mod allows for either randomized or user-configurable arrival time when starting a new game.

The timescale for a new game can also be configured. For reference, when configuring the timescale:
Morrowind default is 30, Skyrim default is 20, real time is 1.

[b]Features & Functionality:[/b]
[list]
[*]All settings apply exactly once, when starting a new game. The timescale setting will persist so long it isn't changed later by another mod or by console command.[/*]
[*]Optionally Randomize your arrival time when starting a new game (Default).[/*]
[*]Optionally limit randomization to Dawn, Day, Dusk, and Night.[/*]
[*]Optionally disable randomization in settings, and instead, select an exact offset for your arrival time when starting a new game.[/*]
[*]Optionally adjust the timescale when starting a new game.[/*]
[*]Settings can be configured from the settings menu on the title screen, before starting a new game.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Requirements:[/b]
[list]
[*]OpenMW 0.51 or later.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Compatibility:[/b]
[list]
[*]The time change is all handled in Lua, and only runs once when starting a new game. This should be compatible with all alternate start mods.[/*]
[*]If you were previously using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46332]Timescale Change[/url], it can be uninstalled, as Arrive Whenever now replaces its functionality. Having both installed won't break anything, but Arrive Whenever's timescale choice will take precedence if it's enabled. [/*]
[*]Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52462]Dynamic Timescale[/url] as of v0.3.[/*]
[*]Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57526]Sun's Dusk[/url] as of v0.5[/*]
[/list]

name: Solstheim Rumor Fix - Fixed - Fixed
author: Multiple Authors
description: Restricts Solstheim dialogue options and rumors. Now only Jonus Maximus, NPCs who are Agents, and the people of Solstheim and Khuul will talk about Solstheim. Unique dialogue added for Nords.
usage_notes:
A few years ago Illy released a [url=http://mw.modhistory.com/download-21-13960]mod[/url]﻿ which restricted the topic Solstheim and the latest rumors associated with Solstheim to a handful of NPCs, and later [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/60629711]nomoresam[/url] released a [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46208?tab=description]fix[/url]﻿ for it. Since according to the description of these mods they can be modified and used freely, I made this improvement, which aims to fine-tune them even more.

[b]What did their mod do?

[/b]- The only Imperial Legionnaire now whose son was stationed at Fort Frostmoth is Jonus Maximus
- Besides him only S'Virr, agents and residents of Khuul know about the place, so nobody else talked about "Solstheim" and the "latest rumors" associted with the place

[b]What is my contribution to the mod?

[/b]- It adds unique dialogue to Nords who are also residents of Khuul or belong to the agent class. There are four nords in Khuul, and several Nords who are also agents. I think that it wouldn't make sense for them to call Solstheim "a terrible place," especially because in [b]vanilla [/b]dialogue, Solstheim Nords tell you that this place is nothing compared to Skyrim. Expect TES V: Skyrim terminology, in which they call everyone who considers Solstheim to be harsh a "milk drinker," or claim that Solstheim is a place for true men to prove their mettle.

[b]Does this mod require the mod made by Illy and nomoresam?

[/b]- No, it's a fine-tuned version of their mod, which contains all the features their mod had, along with my improvements. You only need this file.

[b]Are there any bugs or issues?

[/b]- None that I'm aware of.

[b]Is this clean?

[/b]- Like the melting ice of Mortrag Glacier.

[b]Is this compatible with Rebirth?

[/b]- Yes.

[b]I don't like your mod because of [reasons].

[/b][url=https://youtu.be/xLnTWxpTQt4?t=13]https://youtu.be/xLnTWxpTQt4?t=13[/url]

name: Morag Tong Attacks
author: GrumblingVomit
description: Now the Morag Tong will hunt the player if certain conditions are met.
usage_notes:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/wgqxwAU.png[/img]﻿[/center]

Think it's odd that there's a legal assassination practice in Morrowind, yet no matter how much trouble the player causes, there's never a writ for the player? If so, you're on the right mod page.

Features:
-If the player meets certain conditions, they will be assaulted by the Morag Tong in the same manner as Tribunal's Dark Brotherhood.
-Like the Dark Brotherhood, there are 5 ranks of assassins that are based on player level.
-There are multiple NPCs with leveled items for each rank, so there will be some variety in the attacks.
-Support for various mods to make the assassins use gear from said mods

Conditions
[spoiler]
[list]
[*]If the player has a bounty of 500 or more, there is a chance the Morag Tong will attack on rest.[/*]
[*]If you are a high-enough level to fight the level 20 or level 30 Morag Tong assassins, you may be attacked by more than one.[/*]
[*]If you are rank 8 or 9 of the Morag Tong, you will never be assaulted.[/*]
[*]Mournhold, Sotha Sil, and a few other plot-sensible locations are safe from Morag Tong attacks.[/*]
[*]If you clear your bounty, you will no longer be assaulted.[/*]
[*]If you complete a quest for a great house in a manner that would upset another great house, the Morag Tong will come after you once per quest.[/*]
[*]The Morag Tong only operate within Morrowind, so Solstheim and Cyrodiil are safe.[/*]
[*]Includes an optional plugin that requires that the player be a member of one of the great houses and climb the ranks a bit before they can be attacked.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

Plugins available for the following mods:
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51144]Heins Morag Tong Armors[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/50738]Morag Tong Equipment Diversity[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47041]Morag Tong Polished[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55163]Web of Mephala Morag Tong Headquarters[/url][/*]

[/list]Each rank is visually distinct and will use equipment from any of the supported optional mods you have installed.

name: Djangos Dialogue - Tamriel Rebuilt patch
author: Jonado
description: Patch to incorporate some of Djangos Dialogue into Tamriel Rebuilt.
usage_notes:
With the 22.11 update of Tamriel Rebuilt and version 9 of Tamriel Data, new dialogue filters have been added to prevent most of the general dialogue (more specifically, dialogue with NoLore filters) from the base game to appear on the mainland. The reason for doing so was that some of the dialogue is too Vvardenfell centric. Thanks to the tremendous effort of two Tamriel Rebuilt members, all dialogue that makes sense to appear on the Mainland - and sometimes in the other provinces - were instead copied into TR_Mainland or Tamriel_Data with the new filters. However, a drawback is that general dialogue from other mods will not appear on the Mainland, either.

One such mod is Djangos Dialogue, which enriches the Vanilla dialogue, and adds a lot of dialogue that makes sense on the mainland as well (and quite a lot that doesn't). This mod copies the relevant dialogue and applies the new filters to it. Some of it will also appear in the other provinces (i.e. Skyrim - Home of the Nords and Province Cyrodiil), but in my opinion not enough to motivate a standalone patch. I have tried to preserve the original dialogue lines as far as possible, but sometimes slight modfications were necessary to fit the new setting.

Acknowledgements: I would like to thank [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/40926435]Von Djangos[/url] for writing the original dialogue and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/77253]Alvazir[/url] for fixing various bugs with the original mod. I would also like to thank [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/881270]Evil Eye[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/38286905]Rakanishu[/url] from the TR team for their work with the new NoLore system, and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/64030]Greatness7[/url] for the [b]tes3conv[/b] tool.

name: FMI - Misc
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Fixes a handful of small inconsistencies between lore and what is found in game.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link: 
[/b][/size][size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695 [/url]**[/b][/size]

This mod fixes all the little inconsistencies from my ongoing[url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/1R3UIMR9uRg-tThGqHR9uzF1biQnvOiztBHc2I1so_Pw/edit?usp=sharing] inconsistencies project[/url]﻿ that are too small to warrant being their own separate mod.

[u][b][size=3]Grazelands[/size][/b][/u]

[list]
[*]The Grazelands are described as both arid and as having regular rainfall. See Item C-003 [url=http://www.theassimilationlab.com/forums/topic/16025-uniformity-mods-for-mw-gameplay-vs-text/]here[/url]. Grazelands have a 10% chance of rain, whereas the Ascadian Isles only have a 5% chance. So, gameplay suggests that developers went with the regular rainfall concept.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Vvardenfell and Geography of Vvardenfell
[/i]
[color=#ea9999][size=3]Except for the settled southwest, Vvardenfell is covered by hostile desert wastes, arid grasslands, and volcanic badlands, and thinly populated by the nomadic Ashlander tribes.[/size][/color][size=3] 
[/size][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]Except for the settled southwest and the Grazelands of the northeast, Vvardenfell is mostly covered by hostile wastes and volcanic badlands, and thinly populated by the nomadic Ashlander tribes.[/color]
[/size]
[i]Topic: The Dark Elven Curse[/i]

[size=3][color=#ea9999]In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derives from 'the Dark Elven Curse,' which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the northeastern wastelands, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in the Dunmer's own accounts of their past.[/color]
[/size][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derives from 'the Dark Elven Curse', which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the ash wastes, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in the Dunmer's own accounts of their past.
[/color][/size]
[list]
[*]The Grazelands are also said to have NO roads or tracks, there are obviously some tracks through the Grazelands.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Grazelands [/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]There are no roads or tracks in the Grazelands, but travel is easy across the rolling plains.
[/size][/color][color=#b6d7a8][size=3]There are no paved roads in the Grazelands, but travel is easy across the tracks and rolling plains.
[/size][/color]
[list]
[*]Tel Fyr is described as being in the Grazelands. It is nowhere near the Grazelands.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Grazelands[/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]Permanent settlements in the Grazelands include Vos village and the towers of Tel Vos and Tel Fyr.
[/size][/color][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]Permanent settlements in the Grazelands include Vos village and the tower of Tel Vos.

[/color][/size][b][u][size=3]Coastguard Cutters

[/size][/u][/b]NPCs will tell you that there are Coastguard cutters docked at Seyda Neen who control smuggling along the coast. There are two problems with this, firstly there are no Coastguard cutters present in game, docked at Seyda Neen or otherwise. Secondly, NPCs who are not in Seyda Neen will refer to the cutters being docked "here" when asked about Seyda Neen, rather than "there".

I do not consider it inconsistent to reference something that the player can't encounter in-game, on the contrary I think this can help with world building. But when it is explicitly stated that something can be found in a location here and now, when it can't, just seems confusing. As such, this is my fix:

[i]Topic: Seyda Neen (Filtered for Gnaar Mok)[/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]The Coastguard cutters of Census and Excise docked here control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.[/size][/color]
[color=#b6d7a8][size=3]The Coastguard cutters of Census and Excise who dock there control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.

[/size][/color]Other responses to the Seyda Neen topic are edited accordingly.

[size=3][b][u]Herd Animals
[/u][/b][/size]
When inquiring about herd animals you will be told:

[color=#ea9999][size=3]The two most common herd animals of the Ashlanders are the guar and the shalk. The guar is a large biped, trained as a beast of burden, and raised for meat and hides. Wild guard are encountered in the wilderness; they're usually quite peaceful. The shalk is a large, unaggressive beetle, raised for meat and resin from its shells.

[/size][/color]It is mentioned that wild guar are usually quite peaceful and that shalk are unaggressive. In game both of these animals are aggressive. I have checked every book and piece of dialogue containing the word "guar" and containing the word "shalk". I cannot find any reference to guars being anything other than peaceful. I did, however, find references to shalks being aggressive. This, couple with the fact that we do meet docile guars in game, lead me to fix these two inconsistencies by making wild guar peaceful, as described, and updating the line like so: 

[size=3][color=#b6d7a8]The two most common herd animals of the Ashlanders are the guar and the shalk. The guar is a large biped, trained as a beast of burden, and raised for meat and hides. Wild guars are encountered in the wilderness; they're usually quite peaceful. The shalk is a large beetle, raised for meat and resin from its shells.[/color]

[b][u][size=3]Temple Attributes[/size][/u][/b]

The Tribunal Temple faction's favored attributes are Personality and Intelligence and yet it is inferred in the book "Fellowship of the Temple" that their favored attributes are Personality and Willpower.

[color=#ea9999][size=3]Those who follow the Tribunal must have the Personality to lead others and the Willpower to resist the world's temptations.[/size][/color]
[color=#b6d7a8][size=3]Those who follow the Tribunal must have the personality to lead others and the will and cunning to resist the world's temptations.[/size][/color]

This leaves it compatible with any mods that might correct this inconsistency by changing the Temple's favored attribute.

[/size][u][b][size=3]Ajira[/size][/b][/u]

[list]
[*][size=3]Ajira sends you on a mages guild quest to find, among other things, four samples of heather and willow anther. [/size]
[/list][i]
"Yes, Ajira must study flowers now. Ajira needs samples of Gold Kanet, Stoneflower Petals, Willow Anther, and Heather. These can all be found on the shores of Lake Amaya." 

[/i]Ajira has 5 restocking copies of Willow Anther and Heather that you can buy from her, and she will accept the ones you've bought from her for the quest. 

This mod simply removes those flowers from her inventory so she can no longer sell them to you. 

Thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/4709296?tab=user+files]Gavrilo98[/url] for reporting this inconsistency. If anyone is interested in a stand-alone fix for this, with a re-balancing twist, check out his mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47585]here[/url].

[list]
[*][size=3]Galbedir and Ajira have bet who first advance to journeyman rank however Galbedir already has journeyman rank. Also worth noting is that Ajira has rank of associate.[/size]
[/list]
In v1.1 I changed both character's rank to Apprentice, 1 below Journeyman. Thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/2104994]zelazko[/url] for the suggestion.

[b][u][size=3]Gravedust[/size][/u][/b]

[url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Gravedust]Gravedust[/url] is described as a "spirit-affinitive dust taken from remains buried in consecrated ground." Gravedust cannot be taken from remains and is only found very rarely on consecrated ground. So I made it find-able in burial urns that would usually only contain bonemeal. Now there is a 50% chance to find bonemeal and a 50% chance to find gravedust.

Please note, this change is not included with the main file and is it's own plugin in a separate download here.

[b]Installation[/b]
[size=3][left]Get it in your Data Files folder, activate it in your launcher, and keep it fairly high up the load order so other things can overwrite it if they need to. I've re-dated it so it should be fairly high up by default for vanilla engine users. If you use Patch for Purists make sure FMI_Misc loads after it, which again, it will by default in the vanilla engine.[/left][/size][center][u]Other Mods in the Finished Morrowind - Inconsistencies Series[/u]

name: FMI - Athyn and Shardie
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Makes Athyn Sarethi and Shardie's appearances more closely match what is inferred from the in-game book "The Hope of the Redoran".
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link: 
[/b][/size][size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695 [/url]**[/b][/size]

From "[url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Lore:The_Hope_of_the_Redoran]The Hope of the Redoran[/url]":

"Many, many years ago, a male child was born into House Redoran"

The boy was named Andas.

"His worst enemy was his cousin [b]Athyn[/b], who had borne much abuse at the hands of Andas."

"[b]Athyn [/b]had been sent to Rihad to complete his education"

"When [b]Athyn [/b]returned from [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Lore:Hammerfell]Hammerfell[/url], it was because of the death of his father, who had also been a councilor of the House. [b]Athyn [/b]was old enough to take his seat in the Council"

"[b]Athyn [/b]exercised his right to combat his cousin for the seat."

"[b]Athyn [/b]and his friends were discussing the duel morosely when one of his old teachers, a warrior called Shardie, came into the hall. "

[center]---------------------------------------------------[/center]

The book seems to infer that the Redguard named Shardie was an accomplished fighter and teacher before Athyn Sarethi was old enough to take his seat in the Council of House Redoran. 

I do not know exactly how old is old enough to take a seat in the Council, if anyone does please let me know, but it seems to me that Athyn was a relatively young man during the events of this book. 

As far as I know Redguards have pretty much IRL human life expectancy, whereas [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Interview_with_a_Dark_Elf]Dunmer live much longer[/url]﻿. 

In game, Shardie appears as a young woman and Athyn as a very old man, this seems highly unlikely to me so this mod changes their faces to better match the lore behind the characters, Athyn now appears younger and Shardie appears old.

name: FMBP - Michael Michael Michael
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Fixes Michael Mack's misreadings of the word "Dunmer".
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695[/url] ﻿**[/b][/size][u]

Description[/u]

Four out of the five times that male Redguards speak the word "Dunmer", Michael Mack pronounces it "Dumb-ner".

[i](Before you start quoting lore about historical rivalries between the two races; it happens on the high disposition greetings as well, and the only time he gets it right is on one of the lowest disposition greetings for when the player character is Dunmer.)
[/i]
So I took to Audacity to try and fix it. This was like trying to thread a needle with a sledge hammer.

I reached out to Mr. Mack to see if he would be interested in re-recording the lines. He didn't respond.

So finally I decided to go at it hammer and tongs with Adobe Audition and a demo version of Rx7 Advanced. This did the trick.

[u]Installation[/u]
[left][/left]
This is a pluginless replacer for the sound files so you can just stick it in the same folder as the originals and let it overwrite (making a backup first is always smart) or do it the OpenMW or Mod manager/organizer/mash type thing way.

While you're downloading the mod, listen to Don Ross:


[youtube]YkidVP0AcQ8[/youtube][center]﻿[/center]

name: Empty Threats Disabler
author: rot
description: Disables attack voices like "You will suffer greatly" on sneak kills or other instant deaths.
usage_notes:
You sneakily execute a character and they somehow still find the time to declare that you will suffer greatly, expound with confidence on the magnitude of the suffering you are in for, or propose you 'surrender your life to them so that they will end your pain' (while in the process of lying down on their face). No longer.

This had really been bugging me for the past decade.


(note: NPCs still use their attack voices - they are only bypassed on instant kills, using the normal death Hit voices instead. Additional Attack voice fixes included.)

[b][color=red]DISCLAIMER:[/color] in the original engine, the game will still incorrectly give two error messages if a peaceful NPC attacks you straight from their first dialogue greeting. The game proceeds normally if you click "yes" to both. [/b]This is a general engine issue which, as of May 2021, is fixed only by the new [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/26348?tab=files]beta version of MCP[/url]. It is not fixed in the released MCP 2.4.

name: Tunnel Cough
author: R-Zero aka Reizeron
description: Makes Miner class NPCs cough.
usage_notes:
This small mod makes all NPCs of Miner class periodically cough. Spending a lot of time in a mine can't be good for your respiratory system.

Important! Since there are no coughing voice files for beast races in the vanilla game, this mod regrettably wouldn't work with Argonian and Khajiit miners. If you guys have any good cat/reptile cough sound resources in mind feel free to let me know, I would really appreciate it.

You might also want to check out my somewhat similar mod called [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44371]Silent Assassins[/url].

name: Vanilla Voices Unlocked
author: Maars
description: Unlocks the previously Mournhold-exclusive vanilla voiced lines for use across all NPCs (NOT AI Generated)
usage_notes:
A non-AI voice mod by yours truly, crazy right?

I haven't found any existing mod that does this, and I always felt it was a shame that the trove of voiced lines added by Tribunal was relegated to Mournhold cells.
Simply put, this mod removes the cell restriction on them, keeping it on the ones that directly reference Mournhold, Almalexia, and most of the faith/religion lines.
The majority are Dark Elf and Imperial lines, and there's quite a bit of them that refer to various faction ranks.

You can also choose between the Full version and the Faction Greetings version, which only includes the faction-based hellos for better compatibility.

Requirements:
- Tribunal, but you already have that don't you? :P

Enjoy!

name: Faction Voiced Greetings
author: Maars
description: Adds new voiced lines recognizing your rank in Tamriel Rebuilt & Project Tamriel factions, including the new House Indoril faction from TR.
usage_notes:
Something I've always been interested in making ever since the Voice Generator came out, this mod adds voiced Hello lines (the ones NPCs that play when you get close to them) for the ranks of the unique joinable factions from PT and TR.

By unique I mean not simply localized equivalents of vanilla factions, like the province Mages and Fighters Guilds, as those are covered already by TD using the existing Mournhold lines.

If you use the main version of my [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59546]Vanilla Voices Unlocked[/url] mod the lines might not have enough priority to show up, so on its page I've added an alternate version that only includes the faction-related greetings, just like this mod.

These are the currently supported factions, with more to come as PTR adds new ones:
- [b]House Indoril[/b] (Dunmer M+F, Imperial M+F, as per existing House lines)
- [b]Ja-Natta Syndicate[/b] (Argonian F, Dunmer M+F, Orc M, these only play if the NPC is also part of the JNS)
- [b]Kingdoms of Anvil, Sutch, Kvatch[/b] (Imperial M+F)
- [b]Thieves Guild[/b] (Dunmer M+F, Imperial M+F)

[i]Small note[/i]: instead of the usual male dunmer AI voice you've gotten used to for dialogue mods (meant for easy cloning in longer lines), I've actually made my own from the Tribunal mp3s, which in my opinion makes the lines sound much closer to the vanilla voice. This should make the new lines weave more seamlessly with the existing ones.

Requirements:
- Tamriel Data [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59927]HD[/url]/[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44537]SD[/url] (technically doesn't need either PC or TR, but how would you join without them 😜)

Enjoy!

name: Great Service
author: Von Djangos
description: Enables voiced dialogue for shopkeepers that were shipped with the original game but never used.
usage_notes:
Enables over 100 lines of voiced dialogue for shopkeepers that were shipped with the original game but never used.

Although all races and genders recorded lines of dialogue for shopkeepers, for some reason Beth only ended up using the male lines for Dunmer, Altmer and Bretons in the original game.

This mod enables all other races, plus the female lines for Dunmer, Altmer and Bretons.

Beth buried the lines from the original three somewhat, so you wont hear them very often. I've surfaced mine higher in the list, so you're likely to hear them in the way you hear tavern owners or caravaneers say their lines.

Not all shopkeepers will use them, as there are many kinds of shopkeeper and some races don't have specific lines. For instance, Wood Elves recorded lines for being clothiers, and Khajit recorded lines for selling potions and books.

name: Sheep-no-More
author: McChuggernaut
description: There are no sheep in Morrowind, so why should you be hearing them? This fixes that.
usage_notes:
Walking through the Ashlands near Ald Ruhn on a beautiful clear day, I was startled by a very loud and obvious sheep bleat that came out of nowhere. It broke my immersion pretty hard. There are no sheep in Morrowind, and I don't think anything else living in the region sounds like that. Besides, the audio file is a VERY obvious recording of a living sheep, not some distorted or human-made noise that might pass for a fantasy world sound. So, I took appropriate measures and replaced the culprit audio file with a re-named copy of another ambient creature sound from that region which was already in the game. I chose a somewhat quiet noise, since it will be occurring slightly more often in-game than it did before, and I didn't want it to be a loud, obvious sound that would be noticeably repetitive.

So yes, just replace the old sound file with the new one, and you get a sheep-free copy of Morrowind. Enjoy!

name: LDM - Balmora Rumour Fix
author: Lucevar
description: Adds an option to refuse Larrius Varro's Bloodbath quest, and edits the filtering on vanilla Balmora rumours so that they don't get overwritten by the Varro rumours. 16+ rumours now appear!
usage_notes:
[center][b]Balmora Rumour Fix + Varro quest refusal[/b]
by Lucevar[/center]

Did you know that Balmora actually has a LOT of responses for the latest rumours topic? Yeah, me neither. The only thing you ever hear about is Larrius Varro and his beef with the Camonna Tong. And since you can't avoid hearing about it, and you also can't turn the quest down, it will just sit in your journal forever if you don't want to do the quest (eg if you're roleplaying a pacifist or a Dunmer nationalist type character).

Well, not any more!

[b]Balmora Rumour Filters[/b]
Instead of the ~4 rumours you hear in vanilla, 16 general rumours are now available, plus lots of faction and NPC specific rumours (try talking to members of House Hlaalu, Heddvild, or Only-He-Stands-There, for example) that got drowned out by the Varro rumours. The Varro rumours will still appear, just MUCH less frequently. Some rumours will only appear once you've progressed past a certain point in the main quest. 

[b]Little Secret filters[/b]
There is an optional esp that changes the filtering on the 'little secret' dialogue of several NPCs who tell you Larrius Varro is looking for you, so that it will only appear if you have a reputation >= 6. Use INSTEAD OF the main esp. 

The NPCs are:
[list]
[*]Bacola Closcius
[*]Ranis Athrys
[*]Fascile Charascel
[*]Traven Marvos
[*]Benunius Agrudilius
[/list]
[b]Larrius Varro's Bloodbath - Quest Options[/b]
This mod also adds the option to turn down Varro's quest. He'll still tell you his little story, and you can still complete the quest by dealing with the bad people later - it just won't clutter up your journal. 

[b]Twin Lamps Legion Rumour[/b]
Finally, there was a rumour about the Twin Lamps assigned to members of the Imperial Legion in Balmora. By default, there aren't any members of the Legion in Balmora, so I assigned that rumour to Moonmoth Legion Fort instead. Requires a reasonably high rank in the Legion (Agent), and a disposition of 50, since the dialogue involves Legionaires admitting some sympathy towards an illegal organisation.

name: Honorable Dagoth - Courtesy of the First Blow
author: Sweezly
description: Dagoth Ur will keep his fucking word.
usage_notes:
Through several dialogue lines, Dagoth Ur offers to let you deliver the first hit on him before your fight, only to turn immediately hostile and chuck a fireball at you. This could be interpreted as him playing dirty, and that he's actually just a bastard who will use whatever means to grasp at victory, sure... In that case, why let you hit him at all then? He's not immediately hostile after all, and it's not like he isn't a God (how can you kill a God?).

I think more than anything that this was just an oversight on Bethesda's part, a leftover script from the cut behavior of other ash vampires where they'd only turn hostile after you engaged in dialogue with them.

The mod removes the 'setfight 100' script that activates during his dialogue, meaning the man is now [s]completely docile[/s] entirely [i]honorable. [/i]Relatively simple mod, perhaps too much so, but I haven't seen anyone care enough to address it, so there.

[u][size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size][/u]
Should be compatible with anything that doesn't edit Dagoth Ur's 'final questions' dialogue topic, and I doubt any mods do.

[center][u][b][size=5]Unique Uniques[/size][/b][/u]
[size=4]By: Anumaril21[/size][/center]

﻿


[u]Contents:[/u]

I. Requirements
II. Description

IV. Installation and Removal
V. Permissions
VI. Credits

[u]I. Requirements:[/u]

- Morrowind

- Bloodmoon

[u]II. Description:[/u]

Over the years, many community members have attempted to partially address the lack of unique appearances for unique armor, weapons, creatures, and miscellaneous items within Morrowind. These efforts were never completed and could be difficult to track down between minor mod pages and lost MMH content; not to mention many were high-fidelity, and weren't a good fit for vanilla purists like myself. I've taken the effort to track down, curate, and edit what designs I could find to blend them as seamlessly as I could with the vanilla game; avoiding simple reskins to the best of my ability in favor of designs that add unique geometry or other interesting aspects like animations. What items were missing, or had clashing/dated designs, myself and others in the community went ahead and created new looks for. Additionally, some vanilla items that shared models with unrelated items were given their own appearance. Where possible, assets were recreated using MOP/Clothing Ground Mesh Fix models as a base, while Creature VFX Restoration fixes were forwarded. 

What's Included: Unique designs for 600+ unique and some named/near-unique armor, weapons, books, lights, potions, ingredients, clutter, and creatures that had generic appearances. Female models are provided for all added cuirasses. A complete list of these with credits is available in the docs section and in the download.

There is also an option for 'More Unique Uniques', these are unique items in Morrowind that had their own models, but have been improved upon in minor ways through animations, particle effects, glowmaps, or edited geometry. These include:

[*]Umbra[/*]
[/list][u]III. Compatibility:[/u]

This mod largely changes models and icons for various vanilla objects, with some placement editing where necessary, and should be compatible with most other mods that don't edit the same elements or make drastic changes to the locations they're placed in. Mods changing item stats should be compatible, with any issues that arise being fixable with a multipatch/merged objects. 'More Unique Uniques' simply replaces the models for most vanilla artifacts, save the Ebony Mail, which is edited to include a female model, if that isn't of interest to you, the .esp can be disabled. Just make sure these .esp load after other mods which may alter any of these items, and it's placed lower in your mod organizer than mods that touch them like MOP or Patch for Purists.

[u]IV. Installation and Removal:[/u]

To install, make sure you first have the dependencies listed, then use the mod manager of your choice.

To remove, simply delete the associated files through said mod manager.

[u]V. Permissions[/u]

This mod is intended to be both a somewhat definitive uniques mod as well as a community resource, as it wouldn't exist without the community. If you're interested in contributing new items, improvements, sheathes, or optimizations feel free to DM me or find me on Discord. Included in the download and docs section is a complete item-by-item credits list. You are free to use and adapt any assets contained here so long as the relevant creators are credited. I've worked on this between projects for years now, so I would appreciate if my work wasn't reuploaded into another compilation, but rather others work with me on this one. You're on your honor.

name: Tamriel ReBalanced - Deadlier Denizens
author: KiraMW
description: Makes hostile Tamriel Rebuilt NPCs fight like they should, with specialized caster archetypes, custom spells, summons, stronger stats, and competent builds.
usage_notes:
[heading][center]TAMRIEL REBALANCED[/center]
[/heading]
[b]Tamriel ReBalanced is a dynamic NPC rebalance for Tamriel Rebuilt's hostile humanoids.[/b]

Using OpenMW Lua, the mod evaluates each NPC's existing [b]level and class[/b] and applies an appropriate package. Spellcasters gain specialized spell sets, defenses and abilities; martial characters receive improved attributes, skills and durability; hybrid classes are strengthened in both areas.

The strength of those changes is based on the NPC's existing TR level. A level 5 bandit receives a modest package intended for early characters. A level 20 warrior is built as an experienced combatant. A level 30 rogue mage can possess powerful magic and defenses appropriate to a rare late-game enemy.

Tamriel ReBalanced keeps TR's existing levels and encounters intact, but ensures hostile NPCs have competent builds that match their level and class. Encounter placement and NPC levels remain where TR put them.

This does [b]not[/b] make NPCs scale to the player's level, and it is not intended as a hardcore difficulty or challenge mod. The goal is simply to make hostile NPCs feel believable and competent, rather than the pushovers they can often be in vanilla TR.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662117-115946061.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]WHAT CHANGES?[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Spellcasters[/b] receive class-appropriate specializations with deliberately constructed spell sets, defenses and abilities.[/*]
[*][b]Martial characters[/b] receive level-appropriate improvements to their attributes, weapon skills, defensive skills and durability.[/*]
[*][b]Hybrid characters[/b] receive both martial and magical improvements appropriate to their class.[/*]
[/list]Dedicated spellcasters are an extensive part of the overhaul. They currently draw from [b]15 different specializations[/b], each built across six level bands for a total of [b]90 specialization and level combinations[/b].

A given Sorcerer, Mage, Warlock, Necromancer or Witch can therefore fight very differently from another member of the same class.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662142-787812940.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]MORE THAN BIGGER NUMBERS[/heading]
Tamriel ReBalanced is deliberately [b]not[/b] a blanket stat multiplier or health-bloat mod.

Health is increased where needed, but survivability is only one part of the rebalance. Weapon skills, defensive skills, attributes, spell selection, regeneration, summons, resistances and other abilities are adjusted according to what that character is supposed to be.
A high-level mage should not simply take longer to kill. They should be a [b]better mage[/b].

Caster archetypes are built as [b]coherent specializations[/b], each with its own offensive tools, defenses, summons or utility. Stronger versions are designed for higher-level NPCs.

Some examples include:
[list]
[*][b]Stormblood:[/b] Shock magic, atronachs and magical defenses.[/*]
[*][b]Daedric Vessel:[/b] Sacrifices its own health to summon increasingly dangerous Daedra.[/*]
[*][b]Antimage:[/b] Silence, Magicka damage and defenses against enemy spellcasters.[/*]
[*][b]Gravecaller:[/b] Overwhelms enemies with increasingly powerful groups of undead.[/*]
[*][b]Spellwright:[/b] Specializes in destroying weapons and armor.[/*]
[*][b]Abyssal Leech:[/b] Drains Health, Magicka, Fatigue and attributes from its enemies.[/*]
[/list]This means even enemies sharing the same base class can present substantially different problems in combat.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662157-1343864506.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]BUILT FROM TAMRIEL REBUILT[/heading]
Development began by examining Tamriel Rebuilt's actual NPC records. TR's hostile population was analyzed by [b]level, class, aggression, attributes, skills and combat role[/b]. Classes were separated into martial, caster and hybrid groups, and the resulting packages were built around the patterns already present in TR. This approach also closely follows Project Tamriel's own encounter-design guidance.

The guiding question was simple:

[b]If Tamriel Rebuilt says this character is level 20, what should a competent level 20 version of this character's class actually be capable of?[/b]
[line]
[heading][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662497-412922151.png[/img]
WHAT SHOULD I EXPECT?[/heading]
Early Tamriel Rebuilt remains approachable. Low-level enemies are more capable, but still appropriate for developing characters.

The difference becomes increasingly noticeable as enemy level rises. Mid-level combatants demand more respect, while TR's rare high-level enemies can finally become the serious threats their placement and level imply.

That also makes the world make more sense. When a village is worried about a dangerous necromancer occupying a nearby ruin, the answer is no longer necessarily, [i]"Why doesn't one of the guards just kill him?"[/i]

Sometimes that necromancer really is someone the guards would rather not fight.
[line]
[heading]SCOPE[/heading]
Tamriel ReBalanced dynamically modifies qualifying Tamriel Rebuilt humanoid combatants through OpenMW Lua. It does not change TR's quests, dialogue, locations or encounter placement, and makes no substantial changes to NPC inventories.

Enemies do not scale with the player.

NPCs above the mod's current level-30 rebalance range are left untouched.

Requires OpenMW.

name: The Missing Class - Mananaut
author: TwilotSpankle
description: There's a missing class in the class triangle, time to fill it!
usage_notes:
Every single vanilla class can be placed in a class triangle. Thief-oritented clases on one end, warrior on the 2nd, mages on the 3rd. 5 classes are perfectly situated in one of these 3 orientations, another 3 are perfect balances of 2, and then the bard is a perfect hybrid of all 3. These are entirely based on the skillset. EXAMPLES. The rogue has an equal number of thief and warrior skills, 5 warrior 5 thief, meaning it's a perfect balance of the two. Assassin's have 6 thief, 3 warrior, and 1 magic skill/s, meaning it's a thief-aligned class with a slight lean towards warrior, and a tad of magic. 

These classes have been mapped out on a class triangle before, I'm not the first to do so, but as far as I'm aware I'm the 1st to make an attempt to FILL IN this missing class that is magic oriented, with a slight lean towards warrior. Below is a list of every class, it's skillset make-up, and where the missing class fits in.

[spoiler]THIEF CLASSES
9 stealth, 1 combat, 0 magic: thief
6 stealth, 3 combat, 1 magic: assassin
6 stealth, 2 combat, 2 magic: acrobat
6 stealth, 1 combat, 3 magic: agent
5 stealth, 3 combat, 2 magic: monk
5 stealth, 2 combat, 3 magic: pilgrim

WARRIOR CLASSES
9 combat, 0 magic, 1 stealth: warrior
6 combat, 2 magic, 2 stealth: knight
6 combat, 1 magic, 3 stealth: barbarian
5 combat, 2 magic, 3 stealth: archer
5 combat, 3 magic, 2 stealth: crusader
4 combat, 3 magic, 3 stealth: scout

MAGE CLASSES
9 magic, 0 combat, 1 stealth: mage
6 magic, 3 combat, 1 stealth: battlemage
6 magic, 1 combat, 3 stealth: healer
6 magic, 2 combat, 2 stealth: sorcerer
5 magic, 2 combat, 3 stealth: witchhunter
[b]new class: either: 5 magic, 4 stealth, 1 combat
OR
4 magic, 3 stealth, 3 combat[/b]

PERFECT HYBRID CLASSES
3 combat, 3 magic, 3 stealth: bard
5 magic, 5 stealth, 0 combat: nightblade
5 combat, 5 stealth, 0 magic: rogue
5 magic, 5 combat, 0 stealth: spellsword[/spoiler]

Below is my reasoning behind every skill I've picked

[spoiler]Spear - Not a single damn class has a spear as a major skill. Once again spear lovers get the short end of the stick. I've made it a major skill
Medium and Light Armor - Douglass Goodall himself has made a mod, [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52896?tab=files&file_id=1000063775]The Mananaut's Message[/url][/b], which allows you to obtain "Royal Mananaut armor", which is light armor...HOWEVER, tamriel_data has a mananaut helmet which is medium armor and assumably future pieces will also be medium. So I chose both
Armorer - I needed more warrior-oriented skills, and I didnt want to overfill this class with a dozen offensive skills, and block doesnt make sense, so I chose armorer. Gotta repair your armor somehow on the moon...
Acrobatics - It's the moon. JUMPY JUMPY!!!!
Speechcraft - Mananaut's are a HELLA unique people to hang out with, when you talk with them you will always have your full attention on their words
All other magic skills - Because magic-oriented class of course[/spoiler]

[b][size=4]RECCOMENDED MODS

[/size][/b][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53710]ARCE All Races and Classes Enabled[/url] - More classes to play from vanilla and tamriel data! And all the cool new TD races of course. Naga Mananaut anyone?
[/size] 
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47115]Sensible Races and BIrthsigns[/url] - I can't play without this mod. Makes slight tweaks to some races that just make sense (Argonians will no longer drown) and birthsigns, cause lets face it some birthsigns are just USELESS

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59240]Prison Transfer Alternate Start[/url] - Now you start your character creation IN the imperial city prisons

name: Fairer Weapon and Magic Experience Gains for Sane People
author: MaxYari
description: Fairifies experience gains without overhauling them. Casting magica-expensive spells or using slow weapons brings more XP, failing a cast or missing a swing still grants a little as you learn from your mistakes. Using conjured gear grants a bit of conjuration XP.
usage_notes:
[size=6][b]✦ Fairer Magic and Weapon Experience Gains for Sane People[/b][/size]

A friendly adjustment of the way Magic and Weapon experience gains work. Doesnt aim to be an overhaul, but rather to simply illiminate some points of contention and unfairness, as well as reduce the dark-side pull of a common ways of exploiting the morrowind xp system for "effecient" skill leveling (quick attack spam, cheap "practice" spells). At the same time it's not an anti-cheese mod, previously "efficient" tactics are either slightly less efficient or as eficcient as before, BUT this mod makes normal skill use in combat more appealing and effective as a means of natural experience gain. The changes are quite succinct and are listed below:

[list]
[*][b]Magic XP scales with spell cost.[/b] Casting a spell that costs 15 or less magica grants 1x XP, while a spell costing 75 or more magica grants 5x XP.[/*]
[*][b]Slow weapons grant more XP per hit, fast ones less.[/b] A dagger hit teaches about 0.6x, a long sword 1.15x, a two-handed axe 1.3x, a bow 1.9x. The exact multiplier depends on a true weapon speed, which is different from the speed displayed in the game since different weapons have different actual speed at 1.0 speed value due to differences in their animation durations.[/*]
[*][b]Miscasts and misses still bring a little XP[/b] You do learn from your failures! Only 1/3 of xp that you would've gotten otherwise and, additionally this exp can not actually level up the skill, you still need to succeed atleast once to get over the level up threshold.[/*]
[*][b]Conjuration XP from bound gear and Alteration XP from shields[/b], being hit while under an Alteration shield or actively using a Conjured equipment - grants extra XP of the appropriate magic school.[/*]
[/list]
Adjustible in setting: Options -> Scripts -> Fairer Magic and Weapon XP.

[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img width=217]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/morrowind_kofi_banner_left_half_bright124.gif[/img][img width=618]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[size=5][b]✦ How to install[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.51 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install and enable [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url], it's a required dependency.[/*]
[*]Install this mod [b]with a mod organiser[/b]: download the archive (or this repository as an archive) and drag and drop it into your mod organiser of choice (e.g [url=https://github.com/ModOrganizer2/modorganizer/releases]Mod Organizer 2[/url] on Windows or [url=https://github.com/grazelandsnomad/nerevarine_organizer/releases/tag/v0.70]Nerevarine Organizer[/url] on Linux). [b]Or[/b] [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url] on how to install mods using the launcher or completely manually (it's also very easy).[/*]
[*]Enable [font=Courier New]FairerMagicAndWeaponXP.omwscripts[/font] in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher, after [font=Courier New]MaxYariScriptServices.omwscripts[/font].[/*]
[/list]
Safe to add to or remove from a game in progress.

[size=5][b]✦ Mod compatibility[/b][/size]

Don't combine it with other mods that scale magic or weapon experience (MBSP, Skill Uses Scaled, NCGDMW's magicka-based progression) - both would scale the same experience. Skill uncappers and level-up overhauls are fine.

Modders: how it works, and its interface, is in the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/blob/main/Sources/DEVELOPMENT.md]technical notes[/url].

[size=5][b]✦ AI disclaimer[/b][/size]

This mod is 95% AI slop, this kind of minor rebalance sounded like a great idea to me, especially in a context of my current playthough and I was not satisfied with the existing solutions (they are either too overloaded or just dont do what this mod does). I also had a paid slopmachine subscription at the time, so slopping this out was fairly straightforward. I am still using this in my playthrough and am quite satisfied with how sublte yet fair the changes are, so I think the mod deserved a right to not just be considered a mere slop. Cheers!

name: State-Based HP - Lua
author: degede
description: A conversion of "Talrivian's State-Based HP" to OpenMW Lua.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
original Morrowind script mod can be found [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52183]here[/url]
[i]"Dynamically calculates your maximum Health based on your current Endurance, Strength, and level, removing the need to prioritize stat gains to maximize Health. The mod applies the vanilla Health formula, but uses current player stats."[/i]

'Talrivian's State-Based HP' had a couple subtle bugs and, being a standard script, provided no configurable options or feedback to help narrow down potential problems. I've re-implementation it in Lua for OpenMW.

Just like the original, this script updates the character's max health any time their strength, endurance, or level changes - using the formula:
( ( Strength + Endurance) / 2 ) + ( ( Endurance / 10 ) * ( Level - 1 ) )

This is essentially identical to the game's original health formula. (with only a minor difference arising from it being applied dynamically if you really want to dig into it)

Issues in the original script:
[list]
[*]How it handled fortify health effects was not correct.[/*]
[*]Health was not recalculated on level up if strength and endurance had not changed.[/*]
[*]Under some rare circumstances, the script would produce a health value that was noticeably lower than it should be (around 15% in a situation I was able to consistently reproduce). I didn't narrow down exactly what was going wrong, but the original script was heavily redundant and kind of messy. This no longer seems to be an issue with this new implementation.[/*]
[/list]What I changed from the original:
[list]
[*]Max health was immediately modified when fortifying or damaging endurance or strength. This is not desirable if you want as-vanilla-as-possible behavior, but some players may have liked that from the original. Strength now uses base value only. Endurance will always consider fortify effects from abilities like The Lady sign (this matches vanilla behavior), but whether or not it considers other fortify and damage effects is now an option.[/*]
[/list]
A simple script menu page is also included:
[list]
[*]toggle the script itself[/*]
[*]toggle if max health should be effected by all fortify/damage endurance effects[/*]
[*]toggle debug output[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW[/color][/size]



[color=#D4D4D8]Thanks to Talrivian for the original mod and mikeprichard[/color] for uploading it to nexusmods.

name: Rest and Sleep Recovery Options (OpenMW)
author: Dahatox
description: Choose which of the three resource stats to recover based on whether you are sleeping in a bed or resting.
usage_notes:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/CBAElYb.png[/img]﻿

[b][color=#ff0000][size=4]Requires OpenMW[/size][/color]﻿﻿[/b][/center][b][size=4]Features:[/size][/b]
- The mod will simply try to restore the Health, Magicka and Fatigue to their previous values following a short delay after sleeping or resting. The delay is customizable.
- There are also separate options for portable beds like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45654]Frostwind[/url]'s Bedroll and Covered Bedroll (these 2 are added by default). So bringing a bed with you might not feel like cheating anymore.

[b][size=4]Known issues:[/size][/b]
- Resting near a bed counts as sleeping for the mod. So for example if you have Health recovery disabled for resting, but enabled for sleeping, then resting close to a bed will recover your health.
[b][color=#ff0000]!!! WARNING !!![/color][/b]
There might be unexpected events that cause the mod to fail, or even mess up your stats. If you find any problem, feel free to make a bug report or write a post, but don't expect me to fix it. Until it works reliably enough for me I won't bother fixing it.

[size=4][b]Installation:[/b][/size]
Extract to your Morrowind Data File's folder
Activate 'rest_and_sleep_recovery_options.omwscripts' in 'Content Files' of OpenMW Launcher

[size=4][b]Configuration:[/b][/size]
Via the 'Scripts' tab in the 'Options' menu.

[b][size=4]Compatibility:[/size][/b]

name: Rafael's Shader Pack
author: Many people
description: Optimized postprocess shader pack for OpenMW, making it look better than ever before while still being very Vanilla-friendly
usage_notes:
[b][i]Shaders of light! Pixels of magic![/i]

[/b]A shader pack for OpenMW, using different shaders I've written or collected, tweaked, enhanced, fixed, optimized and changed in different ways, now in a single convenient place.
Enjoy a quality ambient occlusion to make the world look more grounded, quality anti-aliasing, enhanced lighting and weather effects to bring out the best out of Morrowind, while not changing the vanilla experience, and with a very small performance hit.
[b]
How to install the post process pack:[/b]
0. Make sure you have OpenMW (at least version 0.49)
1. Add RafaelsShaderPack to Data Directories in the launcher
2. Set OpenMW gamma to 1.0 and Minimum Interior Brightness to 0.00 (no need for such hacks since we're using tonemapping!), and ensure shaders are activated (if you use a higher view distance than 10 cells, I'd recommend going to 10, max. Reasoning is that shaders are tweaked for 2-10 cells, and lower view distances will also minimize any LOD or pop-in issues you'd encounter)
3. In-game, press F2 (you might need to enable postprocess from the in-game menu, in which case OpenMW tells you to do that), and move the following shaders from Inactive to Active in this order: [i]HBAO, VAIO, godrays, DIVE, wetworld, tonemap, SMAA [/i](or you can just copy and paste "chain = HBAO,VAIO,godrays,DIVE,wetworld,tonemap,SMAA" in the [Post Processing] section of your settings.cfg)
4. If you want temporal filtering (TAA minus temporal supersampling) or motion blur, then add SMB at the end. If not, skip it.
[b]
How to install the PBR lighting and filtered shadows shaders:[/b]
Check the installation instructions in each download.

[b]How to install the Various Data Enhancements:
[/b]Add as a normal mod, you can check or uncheck individual folders, and activate the related ESPs (if applicable). Core is related, the rest is up to you.

[b]Steps for performance boost:
[/b]Set the in-game water "reflection shader detail" to sky, and let the wetworld water SSR do the reflections instead. Considering this is anywhere between a 10% and 30% boost, it is beyond recommended.
If you're using a high shadow map resolution, it is also recommended to lower it, and to instead use the filtered shadows shaders. Too many users bump it to 4096 in order to get rid of ugly shadows when the actual solution isn't that.
If using a very high draw distance, then probably can be tuned a bit down. Anything higher than the game actually lets you is overkill, and usually leads to more aliasing, LOD issues, long loading times, hiccups, and so on. Nice for some screenshots, but not really for actual gameplay. And yes, other games can do this just fine, but different engines yield different results. 

[b]Performance knobs for shaders (if needed):[/b] 
1. Open the post process menu (F2), to go HBAO, and lower the exterior quality to any of the non-GTAO presets
2. If being near water is causing performance problems, then you can switch off the raymarched water by setting WATER_RAYMARCH_WAVES to 0 in lighting.glsl
3. If you notice a performance impact when using many parallax/height maps, then you can switch off the parallax shadows by setting PARALLAX_SHADOWS to 0 in lighting.glsl
 
[b]Quick guide to AA:[/b]
0. Best to use the enhanced PBR lighting shaders, as they have groundcover edge refinement (and some other tricks), thus severely reducing aliasing and shimmering caused by vegetation. The best anti-aliasing is not creating aliasing in the first place!
1. Ensure that SMAA is set to its default state, and change the resolve method to FXAA
2. If what aliasing you see is actual temporal instability or shimmering, but everything is fine when stationary, then what you need is SMB. The latest version also has a tweakable sharpness parameter, so you can find the sweet spot according to your own motion sensitivity
3. If you still somehow feel like there's not enough AA, then you can enable MSAA in the OMW launcher (called simply "Anti-aliasing"). Try 2x to begin with, it creates enough extra edge data in most cases
[b]Note that this can easily create problems between geometry and sky when using post process shaders. It is crucial that if you enable MSAA, then you also enable the sky rendering in VAIO, and you should also [url=https://pastebin.com/raw/cycxjedH]these[/url] in your openmw.cfg.
Note that adding more[i] post process AA[/i] will not lead "more" or better anti-aliasing! [/b]You're mostly just wasting performance. If AA was as easy as applying multiple types of [i]post processing AA[/i] on top of each other, I would've had an option for FXAA & SMAA together, yet I do not. Just like (almost) all games do not. While there might be some edge cases where doing this might look better, there's also cases where this [i]reintroduces[/i] aliasing.
4. If you want MSAA to also affect groundcover (and other transparent objects) then you need to enable "Use Anti-Aliased Alpha Testing" in the OMW launcher. Depending on your GPU and mods this can be a bit costly

Q&A
Q: My game looks very washed out now, why?
A: Ensure your gamma is set to 1.0. The HDR tonemapping and the other effects should lighten up dark areas enough by themselves. If you feel certain scenes are always too dark (for example not only [i]certain[/i] nights, but [i]all nights[/i]) then open up the tonemap settings (F2 -> tonemap, scroll down) and lower the Minimum Exposure (there's 3 of them, depending on your needs)

Q: But I always had gamma high when I played Morrowind, why change it now?
A: Because gamma is only on your monitor, it won't show up in captures, and it can mess up other stuff. Yes, I know that nowadays you can use a gamma or brightness post-process shader to do the same thing, but it's still better to get brighter colors through actual lighting and HDR correctness, which this shader pack is doing.

Q: How slow is my game going to run when using this?
A: The shaders included are optimized, making any performance hit barely noticeable. If someone can run OpenMW with its water shader enabled, then this pack should pose no problem at all.

Q: I use the same settings and a high resolution texture pack, and your screenshots still look more sharp than my game, why?
A: I also use normal maps as much as possible, and sometimes even specular or height maps. Those make a huge difference. Go download some, and enable the game to use them.

Q: When Android/Mac/MGE port?
A: Unsure. No promises.

Q: What about Steam Deck?
A: While I haven't tested it myself, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667?tab=posts&comment_id=162304987]this post[/url] covers installation.

Q: Anything I can do so torches and other lights don't constantly "flicker"?
A: This behaviour isn't from the shaders, it's tied to the lights themselves, so nothing I can do on my side. But, luckily, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55371]this mod[/url] updates them so they their radius is frozen in time.

Q: Any incompatibilities with other mods?
A: No, as far as I've tested. If you are using any other shader and/or post processing mods, make sure mine is loaded last so it can overwrite any old shaders. Exception are other modifications to the core OpenMW shaders! Do not try to mix and match, the optional files provided here are meant to be applied over default OpenMW shaders! Exception to the exception are mods that either clearly state compatibility, or are made specifically using these shaders as a base. Hope this isn't confusing!

Q: Any other incompatibilities?
A: There shouldn't be. But there could always be a weird combination of OpenMW version, operating system, graphics card and/or driver that can lead to either a shader not working at all or causing artifacts. If this happens to you, please post details (OMW version, graphics card used, in-game log with F10, how the problem can be reproduced, etc) and I will investigate.

name: Immersive Eyes-Body Reactions (OpenMW)
author: zenocite
description: OpenMW Immersive Eye/Blink, Yeah I know how this sounds. Blinking, in a video game? Feels like a joke mod at first glance, I get it. But give it a shot before you write it off. Once you've played with it a bit you actually start to notice when it's gone. Not just a cosmetic thing, it actually ties into gameplay too.
usage_notes:
[color=#f1c232][size=4][b]OpenMW Immersive Blink[/b][/size][/color]

Yeah I know how this sounds. Blinking, in a video game? Feels like a joke mod at first glance, I get it. But give it a shot before you write it off. Once you've played with it a bit you actually start to notice when it's gone. Just make sure to check all the extra features in the options!
The idea started with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/54864?tab=posts]Immersive Blinking[/url], full credit to the original creator for planting the seed. This is a full rebuild from scratch for OpenMW 0.51+ using native Lua, not just a cosmetic thing, it actually ties into gameplay too.

[color=#f1c232][size=4][b]Reactive mode[/b][/size][/color] is worth calling out specifically, since it changes what blinking actually is in the mod. By default your character blinks naturally on their own the whole time, ambient and constant. Switch to Reactive mode instead and that idle blinking turns off completely, blinking only happens when it actually means something, getting genuinely exhausted, staring into a storm, clearing the blur after surfacing from water. It turns blinking into a real feedback loop instead of background flavor, a way of reading your character's actual state without opening a menu.

[img width=418]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788054030-52117301.gif[/img][img width=420]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788125538-605291720.gif[/img]
[heading][color=#f1c232]What it does[/color][/heading]
Your character blinks on its own, randomized so it doesn't feel robotic. You can tune the timing however you want in the settings menu, remap the manual blink key through the normal controls menu, and set your own eyes-closed color, grey and black options both available.
It also reacts to stuff around you features down below!

[heading][color=#b45f06]Optional: Super Settings Renderers[/color][/heading]
[b][color=#f1c232]Super Settings Renderers[/color][/b] ([url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59673]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59673[/url]) - not required, but cleans up the settings menu a lot. Sliders instead of typing numbers into boxes, easier to adjust, way less bloated looking overall. Works fine without it too, everything just falls back to the normal controls.

[size=4][b]Also check out my other mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60121]Openmw Personality![/url][/b][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788409443-1610818960.gif[/img]

[b][u][color=#f1c232]What's new in 0.4.0![/color][/u][/b]

[list]
[*][color=#ffd966]Storm reactions[/color] ash storms, blight storms, blizzards, and heavy rain now make your character shield their eyes if you're facing into the wind, same idea as the sun squint, complete with objects correctly blocking it[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]A quick flutter-blink[/color] when facing into wind during a storm without your hand raised[/*]

name: Rock The Boat - Dynamic Camera Rocking for OpenMW
author: Leaposter
description: Enables dynamic camera rocking when standing on a boat or rope bridge, and while water walking or swimming.
usage_notes:
[b]Description:[/b]
Rock The Boat is a mod that enables dynamic camera rocking when standing on a boat, in a boat interior, on a rope bridge, while water walking, and/or while swimming.

Not required, but the effect looks and works best when installed along side [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] and the enhanced water shader with raymarched waves from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667]Rafael's Shader Pack[/url].

[b]Features & Functionality:[/b]
[list]
[*]Rocking is directional, based on the player's orientation relative to the boat or bridge.[/*]
[*]Rocking intensity is configurable per-weather-type.[/*]
[*]Rocking can be enabled or disabled for interiors and exteriors independently of one another. [/*]
[*]Rocking can be enabled or disabled for boats, bridges, water walking, and swimming independently of one another.[/*]
[*]There is an "Anti-Nausea" toggle for those sensitive to the rocking motion, which will replace camera roll with camera pitch. [/*]
[/list]
[b]Compatibility:[/b]
Unlike other mods which attempt to animate the boats themselves, this only animates the camera, making it compatible with any and all existing boat mods. If you encounter a boat that should be rocking that isn't, or a boat that rocks on the wrong axis, or a boat that shouldn't be rocking that is, please feel free to report the issue (with the object name) so it can be profiled!

Rock the Boat is fully compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] as of v0.5. Ensure that Rock the Boat is loaded [i]after[/i] Dynamic Camera. Installing Dynamic Camera will further improve interoperability with other mods that alter the camera using its framework.

[b]Recommended Mods:[/b]
A selection of mods that I find pair nicely with Rock The Boat.
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] - Rock the Boat will use Dynamic Camera for camera control, if present.[/*]
