name: Over-the-Shoulder Combat Stance (OpenMW Camera script edit)
author: Ctroost
description: Edit of the OpenMW third-person camera script that allows the player to retain the over-the-shoulder view when entering the combat stance, because I found the switch to a centered view very disorienting.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]This mod allows the OpenMW's third-person camera behavior to be changed so that the over-the-shoulder view is retained when entering the combat stance, instead of snapping to a centered view. The default centered switch can feel a little disorienting mid-fight.[/color]

This is a very simple edit of the [i][b]third_person.lua[/b][/i] script found in [b][i]resources\vfs\scripts\omw\camera[/i][/b] in your OpenMW installation folder. 

If you would like to manually edit the script yourself, remove the following line:
[code]if Actor.getStance(self) ~= Actor.STANCE.Nothing and mode == MODE.ThirdPerson then state = STATE.Combat [/code]
Then change this line:
[code]elseif Actor.isSwimming(self) then state = STATE.Swimming [/code]
to:
[code]if Actor.isSwimming(self) then state = STATE.Swimming [/code]
Save the file and enjoy.

[u]An improved version of the mod was provided by Jazilla, allowing for the enabling or disabling of the over-the-shoulder combat stance at will through the in-game OpenMW Camera script.[/u]
[line]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]
Install like any other mod through the OpenMW launcher. 

Alternatively, if you're using the original version of the mod, you can drop the resources folder into your OpenMW installation folder, or drop the edited third_person.lua file into resources\vfs\scripts\omw\camera. Overwrite the existing file, and you're done.
[line]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW (I haven't tested the edited Lua file on any other versions besides 0.51.0, but it would probably work fine unless changes have been made to the script since older OpenMW versions.)[/color]
[line]
[size=4][b]Credits[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW team for the original script.
Jazilla for providing an improved version of the mod.[/color]

name: TimeHUD - A Clock UI widget
author: lhyacinth
description: A simple mod that displays the current time, date and temperature
usage_notes:
No longer do you need to use the wait menu to see the time, or dispel levitate or waterwalk. This mod is a widget on the HUD that displays the time and date.

[color=#9fc5e8][size=3]features[/size]
[/color]- easily move the widget by clicking and dragging, lock in place
- change color using a full color picker with presets
- left, center, or right text alignment
- date can be shown above or below the time
- multiple date format options including weekday, day, month, year, and combinations of them
- font size can be changed in the settings, alternatively you can click and use the mouse wheel to change the size as well
- click and shift+mousewheel to adjust background opacity in-game
- adjust border thickness, color and padding
- option to only display the time when outdoors
- three time formats: 24-hour, 12-hour (AM/PM), or text (dawn, morning, noon, afternoon, evening, dusk, night, midnight)
- compatible with custom timescales and [url=https://gitlab.com/lhya/sunsdusk/-/wikis/troubleshooting#help-my-temperature-is-200000000000000000000000000]mods that change the date via mwscript variables[/url]
- pure lua, no .omwaddon or .esp required
- lightweight, can be safely installed and removed at any time and placed anywhere in any load order
- localisations for 13 languages: English, German, French, Russian, Polish, Hungarian, Spanish, Italian, Czech, Portuguese, Romanian, Japanese, and Chinese. changing the localisation requires a restart for the settings menu to update into your chosen language, sorry if the translations aren't great I just used google translate

[color=#9fc5e8][size=3]interop[/size][/color]

Set Timescale 15

[size=5][b]⊹ How To Remove Vanilla Enemy Health Bar[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Find [font=Courier New]./OpenMW/resources/vfs/mygui/openmw_hud.layout[/font] (inside your OpenMW folder, not your Morrowind folder!), if you are using a mod replacing/modifying vanilla hud, such as the beautiful [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53267?tab=posts&BH=1]Centered HUD for OpenMW[/url] - look for [font=Courier New]/mygui/openmw_hud.layout[/font] inside the mod folder instead (if you are using a mod manager to install it)[/*]
[*]Open the file with a text editor[/*]
[*]Find an element with a name EnemyHealth ([font=Courier New]name="EnemyHealth"[/font])[/*]
[*]In the "position" property of that element - 3rd number is this element's length - set it to 0 to hide the element[/*]
[/list]
e.g you might find an element that looks like this

[code]<Widget type="ProgressBar" skin="MW_EnergyBar_Yellow" position="0 131 80 12" align="Center Bottom" name="EnemyHealth">
    <Property key="Visible" value="false"/>
</Widget>[/code]
inside position = "..." change 80 to 0. Save the file. Play the game.

name: The Combat Juice
author: MaxYari
description: A layer of subtle "oomph" lovingly smeared all over TES III combat. Does not alter any gameplay mechanics - purely a visual and auditory satisfactorium. If you are sure that Morrowind's combat mechanics are trash - try this before looking for mods to "overhaul" them.
usage_notes:
[size=6][b]⚔︎ The Combat Juice[/b][/size]

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheCombatJuiceOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/logo.png[/img]


A layer of subtle "oomph" lovingly smeared all over TES III combat. Does not alter any gameplay mechanics - purely a visual and auditory satisfactorium. If you are sure that Morrowind's combat mechanics are trash - try this before looking for mods to "overhaul" them.

Videos below also contain all of the recommended mods. Note that with default setting clothing doesnt fly off characters on death and slowmo is not played on every kill (all tweakable in settings, purposefully turned up in 2nd vid):
[youtube]E8iXQvFb4CM[/youtube]
[youtube]GPr29jKNFYI[/youtube]


Rapid-fire list of all the features:

[list]
[*]A subtle camera shake on hits that scales with how hard your hit landed.[/*]
[*]Slow-mo and a post-processing effect on kills and/or at the end of a fight.[/*]
[*]Hit markers and hit sounds, specifically to enhance the feel of ranged/magic hits (previously part of the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56584]Dynamic Reticle[/url] mod, now they're not).[/*]
[*]Held weapon, helmet and boots flying off on kill (and optionally all the other equipment/inventory as well, if you like loot piñatas).[/*]
[*]Pretty spark on armor hits.[/*]
[*]Everything is adjustable in the mod settings.[/*]
[/list]
Requires [b]OpenMW 0.51+[/b] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url].

[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheCombatJuiceOpenMW/main/imgs/head_like_a_hole_banner_left_half_bright148.webp[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheCombatJuiceOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheCombatJuiceOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[size=5][b]⚔︎ (Strongly) recommended mods[/b][/size]

The Combat Juice was developed to create a lovely, immersive [b][i]symphony of destruction[/i][/b] with the following mods:

[list]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52596]ReAnimation v3[/url][/b] - a one-stop shop for making 1st-person animations feel great. [/size][/*]
[*][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera [/url] - a subtle sway of your hands/weapon when moving the camera around and other subtle niceties.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56594]Hit Reactions Animated v2[/url][/b] - much better animated and more varied humanoid hit reactions and death animations.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55064]Mercy: Combat AI Overhaul[/url][/b] - much more engaging and fun NPC AI in combat.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60361]Combat Sounds Overhaul Overhauled[/url][/b] - a one-stop shop for making combat sound great.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://modding-openmw.gitlab.io/openmw-footsteps/]Footsteps[/url][/b] - a one-stop shop for immersive, surface-adaptive footstep sounds. Note that its description says the original mod (Character Sound Overhaul) is required - I believe this is not true anymore, Footsteps now has its own set of sounds, better than the original CSO's.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55508]OpenMW Impact Effects[/url][/b] - particle and sound effects when a weapon swing hits the environment or an enemy. Also great feedback on missed strikes, since it often makes a miss feel like a strike that glanced off the armor. The Combat Juice's sparks fly wherever Impact Effects decides to spark.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59776]Diverse Blood OpenMW Lua[/url][/b] - distinct blood colors for different creatures, and better blood particles.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60272]They Bleed[/url][/b] - blood on the environment.[/size][/*]
[*][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56589]LuaPhysics[/url] - all the features of this mod related to weapons/equipment flying off on kill require this mod.[/b][/*]
[*][size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60196]OpenMW Immersive Sounds - 1st Person Body[/url][/b] - sounds of breathing and strain during combat and on low stamina, as well as shader and camera sway effects, all of which (you have to trust me) actually don't feel garish or out of place. Very tastefully made.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[b]Honorable mentions[/b] (i.e. more a matter of taste, not [i]strongly[/i] recommended):

[list]
[*][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/50240]Nifty Elemental Magic Sounds[/url][/b] - personally my favourite spell sound replacer. Doesn't sound out of place, not stolen from other games (afaik), just crispy and satisfying.[/*]
[/list]
Yet The Combat Juice will work on its own - everything above is merely a matter of my personal taste. [i]You[/i] can make your own choices (I will not judge you, I promise).

[size=5][b]⚔︎ How to install[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.51 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install and enable [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url], it's a required dependency (most of my Lua mods require it now).[/*]
[*]Install this mod [b]with a mod organiser[/b]: download the archive (or this repository as an archive) and drag and drop it into your mod organiser of choice (e.g [url=https://github.com/ModOrganizer2/modorganizer/releases]Mod Organizer 2[/url] on Windows or [url=https://github.com/grazelandsnomad/nerevarine_organizer/releases/tag/v0.70]Nerevarine Organizer[/url] on Linux). [b]Or[/b] [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url] on how to install mods using the launcher or completely manually (it's also very easy).[/*]
[*]Enable [font=Courier New]CombatJuice.omwscripts[/font] in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher.[/*]
[*]Ensure that post processing is enabled: Options -> Video -> Post Processing (in-game) or "Enable post processing" in the "Visuals" tab of the launcher settings. The kill flash doesn't show without it.[/*]
[*][i]Optional[/i]: for weapons and gear flying off on kill, install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56589]LuaPhysics[/url] and enable [font=Courier New]LuaPhysicsEngine.omwscripts[/font]. Without it, everything simply stays on the corpse.[/*]
[*][i]Optional[/i]: for the sparks, install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55508]OpenMW Impact Effects[/url] and put The Combat Juice [b]after[/b] it in the load order - the new sparks replace its spark meshes.[/*]
[*]Settings are in Options -> Scripts -> Combat Juice.[/*]
[/list]
Have fun!

[size=5][b]⚔︎ Good to know[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Gear flying off on kill moves it out of the corpse and onto the floor, so you pick it up from the ground instead of looting the body. Each item (weapon, helmet, boots, other worn pieces, inventory) has its own chance in the settings - set a chance to 0 to leave that item on the corpse.[/*]
[*]To get Impact Effects' original sparks back, delete the [font=Courier New]meshes/e/impact[/font] folder from this mod.[/*]
[*]The look of the kill flash can be tweaked further in the post processing HUD (F2).[/*]
[*]Hit markers are simple definition files in the [font=Courier New]hitmarkers/[/font] folder. To add your own, copy one of them, point it at your textures, and it will show up in the settings (this works from other mods too).[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]⚔︎ Credits[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]The Stupid-Metal hit markers and their sound come from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55075]Stupid Metal Hitmarkers[/url].[/*]
[*]The kill flash is based on the death effect of the Skyrim mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/148388]Sanguine Symphony[/url].[/*]
[*]Spark meshes were generated with Greatness7's [font=Courier New]es3[/font] library.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]⚔︎ AI disclaimer[/b][/size]

I let AI speak for itself:

I'm Claude, the coding AI Max built this mod with. I wrote most of the code, the tools around it and the generated art - the spark meshes and textures, and the diagonal cross hit marker. Max came up with the idea, decided how everything should look and feel, tested it in the game, tuned it and corrected me when I got things wrong. The description above is Max's own; I only fixed the spelling and grammar. Whether the result is classy or sloppy is up to you to judge!

(ew, sounds quite clanker, aint it?)

name: They Bleed -- immersive blood effects -- OpenMW

description: The spoils of war taint your surroundings; your violence now leaves bloodied marks on the environment. Low-HP player/NPCs also leave subtle blood trails.
usage_notes:
[color=#900000][size=6][b]♦ They Bleed[/b][/size][/color]

The spoils of war taint your surroundings; your violence now leaves bloodied marks on the environment. Low-HP players/NPCs also leave subtle blood trails.

[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheyBleedOpenMW/main/imgs/head_like_a_hole_banner_left_half_bright148.webp[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheyBleedOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/TheyBleedOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[color=#900000][size=5][b]♦ How to install[/b][/size][/color]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.51 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install it like any other OpenMW mod and enable [font=Courier New]TheyBleed.omwscripts[/font] in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher. If this is your first OpenMW mod, [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url].[/*]
[*]Settings are in Options -> Scripts -> They Bleed.[/*]
[/list]
The blood comes with PBR maps made for [url=https://github.com/wareya/OpenMW-PBR]Wareya's PBR shaders[/url], so it looks wet and glossy with them. It [i]might[/i] (or might not) look wrong with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667]Rafael's shaders[/url] or other shaders that read these maps differently. If the blood looks off, delete the [font=Courier New]*_spec.dds[/font] files from [font=Courier New]textures/MaxYari/TheyBleed/[/font] (they hold the metalness and roughness). The normal maps ([font=Courier New]*_n.dds[/font]) are fine and can stay.

To uninstall, set "Max Decals" to 0 and save your game first, so no blood is left behind in your save. Then uninstall the mod.

[color=#900000][size=5][b]♦ Compatibility[/b][/size][/color]

[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45368]Diverse Blood[/url] is supported, and so is the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59776]Diverse Blood OpenMW Lua[/url]. Color of the blood on the environment will match that of Diverse Blood if installed.[/*]
[*]Apart from that should be compatible with pretty much anything.[/*]
[/list]
[color=#900000][size=5][b]♦ AI disclaimer[/b][/size][/color]

Made with HEAVY AI assistance. Only this mod's logo was made completely by human hands, and, well, I also picked out myself that little sound that you might hear when the blood droplets hit the environment. The rest was just babysitting a coding AI, testing and correcting. I personally think that the outcome is classy rather than sloppy, but it's up to you to judge!

name: Dynamic camera - Immersive 1st and 3rd person camera effects and target lock -- OpenMW
author: Max Yari
description: Subtle dynamic camera and first-person viewmodel (hands) inertia. More natural movement and jumping.Target lock with shader effects (bokeh) and a sneak shader (vignette). Immersive cell transition effects (bokeh). Experimental strafe camera-tilt effects (disabled by default).Highly customizable.
usage_notes:
[size=6][b]✩ Dynamic Camera[/b][/size]
[color=#ff0000]Click below to watch a video preview[/color]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UHV4UTi0Kd4][img width=385]https://img.youtube.com/vi/UHV4UTi0Kd4/maxresdefault.jpg[/img][/url]

Subtle dynamic camera and first-person viewmodel (hands) inertia for OpenMW. More natural movement and jumping.

Target lock with shader effects (bokeh) and a sneak shader (vignette). Immersive cell transition effects (bokeh). Experimental strafe camera tilt effects (disabled by default). Highly customizable.

Meant to be used with the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56584]Dynamic Reticle[/url] mod, but will work without it.

[i]1st-person animations in the video are from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52596]ReAnimation v2[/url] and MCAR. Circular reticle, HP widget, sneak reticle and hit markers are from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56584]Dynamic Reticle[/url].[/i]

[size=5][b]✩ Features[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Slight headbob when jumping and landing.[/*]
[*]Viewmodel inertia when looking around.[/*]
[*]Visual and sound effects when moving at high speeds (mainly to enhance the feel of big, long leaps).[/*]
[*]Target lock (set the key bind in the script settings) with a neat DOF bokeh shader active only during the lock. Lock distance and switching targets by moving the mouse/stick are adjustable.[/*]
[*]Immersive bokeh/darkening animated transition when entering or leaving interiors.[/*]
[*]Sneak vignette.[/*]
[*]A few [b]extra effects[/b] - cinematic black bars on target lock and camera roll on strafing. They are disabled by default and can be turned on in the settings.[/*]
[*][b]Full Body Awareness tweaks[/b] - if you play with a visible body in first person using the FBA Compatibility folder of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52596]ReAnimation[/url], these tweaks are applied automatically to make the experience more coherent and prevent some visual clipping.[/*]
[*]All of it is adjustable in Options -> Scripts -> Dynamic Caméra.[/*]
[/list]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/DynamicCameraOpenmw/main/imgs/morrowind_kofi_banner_left_half_bright124.gif[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/DynamicCameraOpenmw/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/DynamicCameraOpenmw/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[size=5][b]✩ How to install[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.49 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install and enable [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url], it's a required dependency.[/*]
[*]Install this mod [b]with a mod organiser[/b]: download the archive (or this repository as an archive) and drag and drop it into your mod organiser of choice (e.g [url=https://github.com/ModOrganizer2/modorganizer/releases]Mod Organizer 2[/url] on Windows or [url=https://github.com/grazelandsnomad/nerevarine_organizer/releases/tag/v0.70]Nerevarine Organizer[/url] on Linux). [b]Or[/b] [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url] on how to install mods using the launcher or completely manually (it's also very easy).[/*]
[*]Enable [font=Courier New]DynamicCamera.omwscripts[/font] in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher.[/*]
[*]Ensure that post processing is enabled: Options -> Video -> Post Processing (in-game) or "Enable post processing" in the "Visuals" tab of the launcher settings. The shader effects don't show without it.[/*]
[*]Set a key bind for target lock in Options -> Scripts -> Dynamic Caméra.[/*]
[/list]
Have fun!

[size=5][b]✩ ReAnimation and Full Body Awareness[/b][/size]

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52596]ReAnimation[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56625]Full Body Awareness[/url] are supported. With ReAnimation's FBA Compatibility folder installed Dynamic camera automatically detect the setup and adjusts arms and camera position while looking completely down to prevent (most of the) clipping.

Nothing needs to be set up - the FBA Compatibility folder is detected automatically, and the settings page tells you whether it was found.

[size=5][b]✩ Known issues[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]With OpenMW's 360° third-person camera, if a target is locked while your weapon is not drawn, moving around switches between targets. It only happens with the weapon sheathed and the 360° camera. Can be "fixed" by disabling look-based target switching in setting.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]✩ Credit[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/Foxunder/mods]Foxunder[/url] for investigating and fixing rare camera jitters.[/*]
[*][url=https://gitlab.com/fallchildren]fallchildren[/url] for debugging and fixing issues.[/*]
[*]High-speed blur shader by EpochWon.[/*]
[*]Cinematic black bars shader by [url=https://gitlab.com/vtastek/]Vtastek[/url].[/*]
[*]Vignette shader by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/wazabear/mods]Wazabear[/url].[/*]
[*]Hex DOF (bokeh) shader by [url=https://github.com/wareya]Wareya[/url].[/*]
[*]High-speed wind howling sound by [url=https://nimsound.ru/]Nimlos' Sound[/url].[/*]
[*]Thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/taitechnic]taitechnic[/url] for helping to improve [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/54782]Dynamic Actors[/url] compatibility.[/*]
[*]Thanks to the folks in the OpenMW Discord for name suggestions and overall help and support.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]✩ For developers[/b][/size]

Dynamic Camera exposes a small Lua interface, [font=Courier New]I.DynamicCamera[/font]: hand it a take-over of the camera while your mod drives it, force the tilt effects on, add extra yaw/pitch/roll that stacks with other mods, and limit how far down the viewmodel tilts. All of it is documented in the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/DynamicCameraOpenmw#taking-the-camera-over]git repository[/url]. If you are already reading this on git - just read below.

[size=5][b]✩ Generative AI use disclaimer[/b][/size]

ChatGPT was used to help write the original description, and it's likely that it was used for parts of the code too.

name: Larger Minimap OpenMW
author: Bloodaxis
description: Simple minimap size increase, alternatively in the top right corner.
usage_notes:

name: Completionist - A Morrowind Quest Tracker
author: MrLuckyNumber
description: An in-game checklist interface to track your quest progress. Designed for OpenMW.
usage_notes:
[center]
[size=6][color=#E2D4A8][b]Completionist - A Morrowind Quest Tracker[/b][/color][/size]
[color=#3c78d8][i]If you find this mod useful, consider leaving an endorsement![/i][/color][/center]
[line]
[size=4][color=#E2D4A8][b]Information[/b][/color][/size]
[b]Completionist[/b] provides a lightweight, in-game interface for players who want to keep track of their journey through Morrowind. It adds a checklist window that monitors your quests progress in real-time.

This mod covers [b]475 vanilla quests[/b] from Morrowind, Tribunal, Bloodmoon, and Official Plugins.

Version 2.1.0 was created to accommodate patches for popular landmass mods such as Tamriel Rebuilt, Project Cyrodiil, and Skyrim: Home of the Nords. All patches are available in optional files, under the download tab. In total, [b]more than 1000 quests are covered.[/b]
[color=#f4f4f4]
[i]Notes:[/i][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#f4f4f4][color=#f4f4f4][i]I am aware that a "true" 100% completion in a single playthrough is technically impossible due to mutually exclusive quests. This mod is intended as a tool to help you see how much of the world's content you've experienced.[/i][/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#f4f4f4][color=#f4f4f4][i]It works on existing save games. You do not need to start a new character; the tracker will automatically recognize and mark quests you have already completed.[/i][/color][/color][/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4][color=#E2D4A8][b]Features[/b][/color][/size]
[list]
[*]Press [b]K[/b] (configurable) to pull up the full quest list. Entries are [b][color=#cccccc]gray[/color][/b] by default and switch to [color=#3c78d8][b]blue[/b][/color] the moment you finish them.[/*]
[*]Dedicated counters that monitors your advancement, providing a clear percentage of your overall world completion as you play.[/*]
[*]Hover over any quest to view a quick summary of its goals and background.[/*]
[*]Use [b]Shift + Left Click[/b] to manually mark quests as complete if needed.[/*]
[*]Search bar to filter quests by name.[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4][color=#E2D4A8][b]Compatibility[/b][/color][/size]
This mod is designed to be as non-intrusive as possible. It does not modify any vanilla records or scripts.
[list]
[*]Safe to install at any point in your playthrough.[/*]
[*]Should work with any other mod in your load order.[/*]
[/list]
[i]Note: By default, the mod will not show quests from other mods. To enable this, a patch needs to be created (see the Patching Guide).[/i]

[b][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/Rebelember][color=#d1b072]Rebelember[/color][/url] has tons of patches on [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58523?tab=description][color=#d1b072]Completionist Patch Hub[/color][/url].[/size][/b]

[line]
[i][size=4][color=#E2D4A8][b]Permissions & Patching Guide[/b][/color][/size]
Anyone is free (and encouraged!) to create patches or addons. I only ask that the [b]original file remains a requirement[/b] for your upload. Click the button below to see the tutorial on how to do this.[/i]
[spoiler][i]

To create a patch, simply create a standalone mod folder with a [b].lua[/b] script that sends your data to the main mod via events.

[b]ID Formatting Rules:[/b]
[/i]
[list]
[*][i] [b]Comma ( , )[/b]: Use this if the quest has multiple IDs that must [b]all[/b] be completed (AND logic).[/i][/*]
[*][i][b]Dash ( - )[/b]: Use this if the quest has multiple IDs that are mutually exclusive or if [b]only one[/b] is required to complete it, such as different quest paths (OR logic).[/i][/*]
[/list][i]

[b]Example Code Structure:
[/b]
[/i]
[code]
local self = require('openmw.self')
local myCustomQuests = {
    {
        -- Simple ID example
        id = "Fictional_Quest_ID_01",
        name = "The Mystery of the Missing Spoon",
        category = "Epic Quests",
        subcategory = "Town Mysteries",
        text = "A local baker has lost his favorite spoon.",
        master = "Your Amazing Mod",
    },
    {
        -- Multiple required IDs (Player must finish BOTH)
        id = "Fictional_Part_A, Fictional_Part_B",
        name = "The Ancient Trial",
        category = "Epic Sagas",
        subcategory = "Trials",
        text = "Complete both the Trial of Fire and the Trial of Water.",
        master = "Your Amazing Mod",
    },
    {
        -- Multiple paths/Exclusive IDs (Player finishes EITHER A or B)
        id = "Quest_Path_Good - Quest_Path_Evil",
        name = "A Fork in the Road",
        category = "Epic Sagas",
        subcategory = "Choices",
        text = "Decide the fate of the village through either path.",
        master = "Your Amazing Mod",
    },
}
local hasSent = false
return {
    engineHandlers = {
        onUpdate = function(dt)
            
            if not hasSent then
                print("[Completionist] Sending quest data...")
                
                self:sendEvent("Completionist_RegisterPack", myCustomQuests)
                
                print("[Completionist] Data sent successfully!")
                hasSent = true
            end
        end
    }
}[/code][i]

[/code]

[b]Final Steps:[/b]
You must include a file named [b]YourPatchName.omwscripts[/b] in your mod folder with:

[/i]
[code]PLAYER: scripts/YourModFolder/my_patch.lua[/code][i]

Your mod's folder structure should look like this:

[/i]
[code]YourPatchName/
├── YourPatchName.omwscripts
└── scripts/
﻿└── YourPatchName/
﻿   ﻿└── my_patch_quests.lua[/code][/spoiler]

name: QuickSelect Ultimate - OpenMW (Full Gamepad - Keyboard - Mouse support) Quick Select Hotkey Hotbar Actionbar
author: skrow42
description: FULL GAMEPAD - KEYBOARD - MOUSE SUPPORT Ultimate Quick Select for OpenMW. Boost your QuickSelect into year 2030
usage_notes:
# QuickSelect Ultimate v1.6 - OpenMW

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/54587]First made by SkyHasACat[/url]
The mod had gamepad support which I was looking for but the visuals seemed so incomplete as you can see on screenshots there. That had to be fixed since the mod looked discontinued.
I have took the time to maximally polish the mod and make it suitable for every user - keyboard and/or mouse or gamepad. Fixed the visuals as well and added new options to separate out the enabled controls. Added spell icons in the quick action spell pick list. Also added expandable lists in the spell list. Added new possibilities of intuitive controls.

Looking at other Quick Select mods available out there (respect to all the authors, of course), this one has the potential to be the one, considering what it has to offer.

## Hotbar Usage

[b][size=5]F1 brings the Quick Select Menu (this is replacer for Vanilla quick select)[/size][/b]

Keyboard 1-10 Hotkeys are on by default:
Shift + 1/2/3 swaps between hotbars 1,2,3 by default. You can change that in the settings.

If Mouse controls are enabled:
You can bring hotbar visible by using Mouse Wheel Down
Mouse Wheel Down also skips to the next right position of the hotbar
Mouse Wheel Up swaps between 1,2,3 Hotbars
Mouse3 (clicking mouse scroll) activates selected Hotbar item

If Gamepad controls are enabled:
To wake up hotbar controls press either DpadRight or DpadDown
To navigate hotbar you can press DpadUp/Down to change 1,2,3 Hotbars and DpadLeft/Right to navigate the hotbar
To choose a hotbar item, press X (or Xbox A)

The rest of the controls are listed in the Quick Select windows.


## Installation

1. Download and extract the mod files.
2. Extract the contents to your chosen file path (e.g., `C:\Users\YourName\Documents\My Games\OpenMW\data`).
3. Launch OpenMW and enable 'QuickSelectUltimate.omwscripts' in the Data Files section of the launcher. Put it preferably at the end of the load order to avoid any potential problems.
4. Launch the game, go into the mod options to set it up completely and enjoy.

## Settings

Access the mod settings in the OpenMW launcher under Settings > Mod Settings > QuickSelectUltimate.

- **Show Next and Previous Hotbars**: Preview adjacent hotbar pages.
- **Show Hotbar at All Times**: Always display the hotbar or only when selecting.
- **Enable Mouse Controls**: Toggle mouse wheel and middle mouse button controls.
- **Enable Gamepad Controls**: Toggle DPad and button controls.
- **Unequip When Selecting Equipped Items**: Toggle auto-unequip.
- **Show Numbers for Empty Slots**: Display slot numbers on empty slots.
- **Pause While Selecting**: Pause the game during selection.
- **Use Arrow Keys for Selection**: Enable arrow key navigation.
- **Set Hotbar on Top**: Position the hotbar at the top of the screen.
- **Bar Selection Key**: Choose key combination for page switching (Shift/Ctrl/Alt).

## Compatibility

- Requires OpenMW 0.49+
- Compatible with most mods, but will probably conflict with other hotbar or UI mods.

## Credits

Big thanks to SkyHasACat for his base mod which was a great foundation for me to work on and make it better.

name: Less Awful Pauldrons
author: uMkNfC4zxfe8Gh
description: A mesh replacer for some of Morrowind's vanilla pauldrons. The aim is to bring ES3's comically large pauldrons in line with both the low-slung style of the original concept art and physics in general. I have tackled what I viewed as the biggest offenders, mainly the most common armors and guard attire.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Fomod Installation Instructions[/b][/size]
Select any/all of the individual replacers in the fomod menu.

[size=4][b]Manual Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8][size=3]Unzip the file and move the contents of "00 - merged" directly into the "Data Files" folder. Individual replacers can be found in the other folders and installed separately.[/size][/color]

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]This mod replaces the pauldrons for several of the vanilla armor sets. I took inspiration from the concept art, where the armor makes a more low-slung silhouette. And more importantly I wanted to make the vanilla guards look less like they have gravity-defying vestigial wings.[/color][/size]

[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]The sets addressed are listed here, more may come in the future:[/color][/size]

[list]
[*]Netch Leather[/*]
[*]Chitin[/*]
[*]Bonemold[/*]
[*]Bonemold - Armun-An[/*]
[*]Bonemold - Gah-Julan[/*]
[*]Indoril[/*]
[*]Steel[/*]
[*]Dwemer[/*]
[*]Orcish[/*]
[*]Iron[/*]
[*]Her Hand's[/*]
[*]Imperial Chain[/*]
[/list]The existing options for pauldron replacers are not actual mesh edits, instead being simple rotation/scales of the original assets. These new meshes are hand-made morphs designed to look more reasonable and eliminate clipping (as much as possible). Unfortunately, I designed the meshes with a few specific clothing interactions in mind, so some of the larger robes do clip through.

As of the newest version, the steel and iron cuirasses have been altered slightly as well to reduce clipping. The iron cuirass was especially tubby.

[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]None[/color][/size]

name: Mercy - Combat AI Overhaul
author: Max Yari
description: An immersive overhaul of in-combat NPC behavior for OpenMW 0.51+. With new voice lines (optional) and animations. Rich on memorable encounters and engaging fights.
usage_notes:
[b][color=#ff0000]INSTALL THE DEPENDENCY OR IT WILL NOT WORK (It's a new dependency now) :)[/color][/b]
[b]
[color=#ff00ff]HAVING PERFORMANCE ISSUES[/color][color=#ff0000]?? [/color][/b][color=#f4cccc](not necessarily on this mod, but in general)[/color][color=#ff00ff] [b]INSTALL[/b][/color][color=#ff0000][b] [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58557?tab=files]Rubic0n[/url] !!![/b][/color]

[size=6][b]☮ Mercy: Combat AI Overhaul[/b][/size]

A significant overhaul of in-combat NPC behavior for OpenMW. Using a custom Lua behavior trees library, with new voice lines and animations. Complete overhauls melee NPCs and partially overhauls spellcasters and marksmen.

The combat doesnt always need to end in bloodshed, but when it does - it does so in [i]style[/i].

NPCs are now capable of more than chasing and stabbing. They will move around, run, walk, execute series of attacks, and use quick and charged attacks interchangeably. They might be cautious to engage or even not willing to fight anymore. Those with spellcasting ability sometimes will use a wider array of spells appropriately (such as invisibility) or even, very occasionally, use few of the very exotic special spells (quite rare, still vanilla friendly, but might be with a dash of humour, you will have to trust my sense of humour here).

The overall goal of the mod is to make the combat more engaging and entartainment as well as introduce some occasional memorable encounters that feel "different" (but not immersion-breaking).

Many new ElevenLabs-generated combat voice lines by [url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/vonwolfe]vonwolfe[/url], currently for Dunmer, Nord and Orc (male and female) and Imperial (male) NPCs. Can be easily turned off in settings if AI slop voices grind your gears (understandably, I like them though).

[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/head_like_a_hole_banner_left_half_bright148.webp[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[size=6][b]☮ Demos and Details[/b][/size]

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/demo1.gif[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/demo2.gif[/img][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO/main/imgs/demo3.gif[/img]

The gifs above show some of the new behaviours.

Now below are lists of behaviours and spells that Mercy adds, I personally consider those to be spoilers and would STRONGLY recommend to just play it and have some sense of wonder. But if you hate surprises read under the spoilers below.

[b]Full(ish) list of behaviours[/b]
[spoiler]

Most of them have some amount of randomisation, so different NPCs might behave slightly (or significantly) differently.

Chances of these behaviours can be increased/decreased in the mod's settings page: Options -> Scripts -> Mercy: CAO.

[list]
[*]Hitting an NPC alerts their friends nearby, the ones who can see it will join the fight.[/*]
[*]NPCs might be unwilling to engage and warn you not to come closer instead (depends on how aggressive they are and how much they like you). Come too close or attack them and they fight. If they lose sight of you - they might come looking where they last saw you, and eventually give up. Guards never hesitate.[/*]
[*]When unwilling to engage they migh go and investigate after loosing a sight of you, or even attempt to sneak up on you.[/*]
[*]Chase, fall back, strafe around in combat, walk menacingly. Rare NPCs will jump around or run around you at full speed.[/*]
[*]Chain attacks together, the max amount of attacks in a chain depends on their weapon skill.[/*]
[*]Make mistakes in picking the best attack type, more mistakes at lower weapon skill.[/*]
[*]Some might get angry when you keep hitting them fast and respond with a war cry and a similar quick attack spam.[/*]
[*]At low health (below 33%, adjustable in the settings) every hit has a chance of scaring them. A scared NPC will either run away looking for friends, or ask for mercy - giving up all the items they carry (except the clothing/armor they wear) and leaving the fight. Guards never surrender, and NPCs don't surrender to creatures.[/*]
[*]Your companions will usually spare enemies asking for mercy.[/*]
[*]NPCs might retreat from an invisible enemy.[/*]
[*]When casting special mercy spells that hinder you in some way - might chose to run away and hide.[/*]
[*]Probably other smaller things that I forgot about.[/*]
[*]Some spellcasters have 0-3 added level-appropriate mana potions which will they drink not more frequently than once in 10-15 seconds.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[b]Full(ish) list of extra NPC spells[/b]
[spoiler]

2/3 of vanilla casters get 1-2 Mercy spells Furthermore, only 1/3 of those get an "Exotic" spell

[list]
[*]Blindness on target (not 100% magnitude but close to it)[/*]
[*](Exotic) Blink - teleports the target to a random (reachable)[/*]
[*]Chameleon 50% on self[/*]
[*](Exotic) Confusion on player - flips your keyboard controls[/*]
[*]Invisibility on self - for repositioning or to run away and hide[/*]
[*]Levitation bolt - 1pt levitation and speed debuff on player[/*]
[*]Light - light on self with a minor agility buff[/*]
[*](Exotic) Pillow fight - shoots out a cone of pillows (yes you heard that right, it looks as great as it sounds, trust me), physical damage, requires Lua Physics to be installed[/*]
[*](Exotic) Skeleton jail - a projectile that spawns 4 skeletons around the target if it hits. Skeletons are very shortlived.[/*]
[*]Speed boost on self[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]☮ How to install[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.49 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install and enable [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url], it's a required dependency.[/*]
[*]Install this mod [b]with a mod organiser[/b]: download the archive (or this repository as an archive) and drag and drop it into your mod organiser of choice (e.g [url=https://github.com/ModOrganizer2/modorganizer/releases]Mod Organizer 2[/url] on Windows or [url=https://github.com/grazelandsnomad/nerevarine_organizer/releases/tag/v0.70]Nerevarine Organizer[/url] on Linux). [b]Or[/b] [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url] on how to install mods using the launcher or completely manually (it's also very easy).[/*]
[*]Enable the mod's .omwscripts file in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher.[/*]
[*]Ensure that "Use navigation mesh for pathfinding" is enabled in the "Gameplay" tab of the launcher settings. It's usually enabled by default, but Mercy can't take over NPCs without it, so it never hurts to double-check.[/*]
[*]Optional: install and enable Lua Physics [TO DO: provide a link] - its only required by a single rare spell that Mercy spellcasters very occasionally can use, its completely safe to not install it, in that case you will wimply not encounter that spell[/*]
[/list]
Note: Previously this mod required a Lua Behaviour Trees 2e dependency; it is not required anymore as it is bundled together with the mod.

Note: The compatibility patches script file (present in old versions of Mercy) was removed on purpose, it's not needed anymore.

Have fun!

[size=5][b]☮ Recommended mods[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59069]Consuming Animated[/url] to make it clearer when mages chug a mana potion.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/54976]Take Cover[/url] by mym - a nice immersion mod that handles enemies fleeing and hiding when they can't reach the player.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55059]One-handed animations and idle fixes[/url] by me - makes NPCs look less stupid when they use one-handed weapons (used in the gifs above).[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52596]ReAnimation[/url] also by me - a good set of first-person animations (if I can say so myself, wink-wink, nudge-nudge) to make the combat feel even more dynamic and less repetitive.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]☮ Credit[/b][/size]

Thanks to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/CYB30]Cybvep[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/zsouza13]zsouza13[/url] for intense testing.

ElevenLabs-generated voice lines by [url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/vonwolfe]vonwolfe[/url].

My thanks also goes to the OpenMW Discord community for massively helping me overcome a multitude of Lua hurdles, testing, and providing feedback.

[size=5][b]☮ Mod compatibility[/b][/size]

Not compatible with most mods directly affecting NPC behavior in combat, unless a mod specifically used Mercy interface to add compatibility.

Mods by [url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/mym]mym[/url] are compatible.

[size=5][b]☮ For developers[/b][/size]

Mercy provides an extension interface for developing new NPC behaviours that get injected alongside Mercy's own (patches for other mods can be made the same way), an interface to take Mercy out of the way for specific NPCs, and a config system to blacklist specific NPCs or whole cells from Mercy or from surrendering, and to keep specific items from being dropped by surrendering NPCs. Mercy's behaviour trees live in [font=Courier New]OpenMW AI.b3[/font], which you can open in the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/behavior3editorplus]Behavior3+ editor[/url].

All of it is documented in the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/OpenMWMercyCAO#adding-mercy-compatibility-to-your-mod]git repository[/url]. If you are already reading this on git - just read below.

[size=5][b]☮ MWSE compatibility[/b][/size]

This is an OpenMW Lua mod, it's not compatible with MWSE. It's probably possible to port it since most of the mod is pure Lua, but I'm not familiar with MWSE and am not planning to change that. If you'd like to port it - feel free to do so. If possible please keep this mod as a dependency.

[size=5][b]☮ FAQ[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Generative AI is evil![/b]
Yea, kind of, but also this is not a question.[/*]
[*][b]Is this compatible with mod X?[/b]
I don't know anything beyond what I described above in the compatibility section. You can always try it and report.[/*]
[*][b]Can I get a version for an older OpenMW?[/b]
No, Mercy relies on Lua functions that older versions don't have. You can keep a separate, newer OpenMW install, you don't need to overwrite anything nor reinstall your mods.[/*]
[*][b]Modding/extension documentation is bad, I don't understand it![/b]
Well, I did my best with it. Experiment and read Mercy's code, I'm sure it's not that difficult to figure out if you really want to extend Mercy.[/*]
[*][b]Do I need to have Mercy as a dependency if I want to make my own behaviour tree mod?[/b]
No, of course not, you don't need Mercy to use the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/behaviourtreelua2e]behaviour tree Lua library[/url] or the visual editor in your projects![/*]
[/list]

name: Npcs and Creatures Rest (OpenMW)
author: lelimule
description: In Morrowind, NPCs and creatures rest (to regain health and magicka) only when the player rests. It isn't realistic. Now they can also rest at any time. They also regain fatigue when player is in another cell.
usage_notes:
[font=Georgia]It's simple: every game time hour, NPCs and creatures rest a little bit if they have health or magicka to regain.

The "rest" is not displayed, it's implicit. The "rest" can be considered as sleep, but also as little care of all kinds. In short, a wounded actor always manages to heal himself a little. No more enemies that stay with the same wounds while player is getting back on his feet at town...

Concretely, every game time hour, NPCs and creatures regain a fraction of health and magicka. For example, if the player wait X hours, wounded actors won't stupidly wait with their open wounds... They will regain some health and magicka.

It respects the Morrowind calculation of health and magicka regain. This mod considers that concerned actors don't spend 100% of their time to rest, only 50%. So the regain is divided by 2.

Morrowind has also a problem with fatigue regain: NPCs and creatures don't regain fatigue when player is in another cell (except when player rests). This mod solve that (thanks to mym for the idea). It respects the Morrowind calculation of fatigue regain.


Recommended mod: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55293]Fair Care[/url] version 3.4.1+ (with my mod, i recommend you to disable the Fair Care "NPCs and creatures health regeneration" option (v3.6+) (for a more realistic gameplay - it's my point of view))[/font]

author: Cybvep
description: Ghostfence now disrupts levitation magic in the Red Mountain region.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]

While the Ghostfence is far from being foolproof, it still stands in-game. As long as that's the case, its magic will keep disrupting levitation in Red Mountain exteriors. Mostly to prevent things from going out, but here of course it's about the player experience. It enforces the Red Mountain theme as a danger zone which the Temple and the Redoran are trying to contain. Once the Main Quest is completed and the Ghostfence deactivated, levitation will no longer be disrupted.

A little bit more reactivity, a little bit more immersion, and a little bit more pain.

No cell edits. Everything is done via script.

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]

The easiest way to install the mod is to unpack the files to a selected folder and append the folder via OpenMW's Launcher (Data Files tab).

This mod was tested on OpenMW. Compatibility on the Vanilla engine can't be assured. It's mwscript, so I assumed it would work if the scripts were recompiled, but I got a report from Sataniel who tested that and it didn't work.

name: Sorry We're Closed - Nighttime Service Refusal
author: Povuh
description: Shops and services are made unavailable at night, with some smart exceptions and lots of new class-specific dialogue! A fully dialogue based mod, no scripting involved. It works automatically for most NPCs added by other mods, and it's compatible with both the vanilla and OpenMW engine!
usage_notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/CBAElYb.png[/img]

⋆⁺₊⋆ ☾⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆⁺₊⋆

[b][size=4]How it works[/size][/b]

Morrowind's NPCs don't follow a day-night schedule, so nightfall has mostly been just a change in lighting.  With this mod you'll actually have to consider the time of day in your plans, as most NPCs will no longer offer you services at night!

From 22:00 to 7:00, most NPCs will no longer offer services like barter, travel, training, spellmaking, or repairs. Each NPC class has unique night-time greetings and service refusal dialogue to signal this. However, you're still able to speak with them about anything else. This mod does not lock doors at night or move any NPCs. 

An alternative [b]Night Travel Mode [/b]is available that keeps all travel services available at night. This can also be changed mid-game with a console command.
[b][size=4]
Special exceptions[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]If an NPC has a disposition of over 80 towards the player, or is at least two ranks below the player in the same faction, they'll make an exception and provide their services.[/*]
[*]Publicans, Pawnbrokers, Guild Guides, Gondoliers, Assassins, Nightblades and Thieves Guild members will continue offering services at all hours.[/*]
[*]Healers, Alchemists and Apothecaries also remain available at night, but only for those who are diseased or severely injured. [/*]
[*]Vampirism: If the player is a vampire, any NPC still willing to offer them services will also do so at night.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]New dialogue[/b][/size]

Each service-providing class now has unique night-time greetings, acknowledging the late hour and clearly signaling whether services are available. This adds a nice bit of immersion, even when speaking to these NPCs for other reasons. All the classes have multiple service refusal lines as well! 

The greetings are given low priority to avoid overriding unique or quest-related dialogue. Some traders, like Arrille and Ra'Virr, likely won't use them because of this. They will still refuse service with appropriate dialogue as expected!

[b][size=4]Compatibility[/size][/b]

This mod will automatically cover NPCs added by mods, as long as they were assigned one of the vanilla service classes.

A Tamriel_Data add-on is available, to cover the new service classes created for Tamriel Rebuilt and the Project Tamriel province mods (bakers, jewelers, potters, etc.). Confirmed to be compatible with the Poison Song update!

Aside from adding new classes, mods can also add services to NPCs with a non-service class. This is sometimes done to bypass skooma trading restrictions. As a result, service refusal coverage for modded NPCs may not always be perfect, though this can sometimes make sense for those characters.


[b][size=4]Switching to Night Travel mode[/size][/b]

If you want travel services to remain available during the night, you can download the version of the mod that is set to Night Travel mode by default. However, you can also use the main mod, and at any point during the game switch to Night Travel mode using the following console command:

[code]set pNightTravel to 1[/code]
If using the Tamriel_Data add-on, make sure to also run this console command:

[code]set pNightTravelTD to 1[/code]
Set the values back to 0 to make travel services unavailable at night again. 
[size=4][b]
Recommended mods[/b][/size]

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58941]Sorry Too Stormy[/url] is the bad weather variant of this mod. Works great together, load order doesn't matter.

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48610]Improved Inns Expanded[/url] will make it easier to find a place to spend the night, until services resume in the morning.

Survival mods like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/49057]Ashfall[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57526]Sun's Dusk[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56480]Devilish Needs[/url] make having to wait for shops to open actually have impact on your character. Luckily because publicans still operate at all hours, you should still be able to buy food and drink at night at most inns. 

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47253]Djangos Dialogue[/url] adds lots of new dialogue, some of it based on weather and time of day. My greetings will take priority over some of Djangos' nighttime greetings, to keep them consistent with the service refusal.

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51427]Real Disposition[/url] will makes it tougher to reach the 80 disposition needed for NPCs to make an exception. I use the Light version.

I personally don't use [url=https://modding-openmw.gitlab.io/go-home/]Go Home[/url], but it should work very well alongside my mod. That way if you manage to find where service NPCs go at night, they will still refuse you service!

[b][size=4]Credits[/size][/b]

name: Sorry Too Stormy - Bad Weather Service Refusal
author: Povuh
description: Outdoor shops and services are made unavailable in stormy weather, with some exceptions and a bunch of new weather-specific dialogue! A fully dialogue based mod, no scripting involved. It works automatically for most NPCs added by other mods, and it's compatible with both the vanilla and OpenMW engine!
usage_notes:

⁺₊⋆❅₊⁺⋆₊⁺ ❅⁺₊⋆₊⁺⋆ ✦⁺₊⋆❅₊⁺⋆₊⁺ ❅⁺₊⋆₊⁺⋆ ✦⁺₊⋆

[size=4][b]How it works[/b][/size]

It's time to head inside! In the following weather types, all services offered by outdoor NPCs (travel, barter, repair, enchant, etc.) are unavailable until the weather clears.

[list]
[*]Ash storms[/*]
[*]Blight storms[/*]
[*]Thunder storms[/*]
[*]Blizzards[/*]
[/list]Services are still offered in normal rain or snow.

The mod features a variety of NPC greetings and service refusal messages referencing the bad weather. You’re still able to speak with these NPCs about anything else.

A blight-only version is available as well, where service is only refused in blight storms.
[b]
[size=4]Special exceptions[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Silt Strider caravaners are well versed in navigating ash storms. Both Silt and Water Striders are also not bothered by thunderstorms. They will continue to provide travel service in these weather types. Boats will not![/*]
[*]Obviously, all indoor services are unaffected by the weather.[/*]
[/list]
[b][size=4]New dialogue[/size][/b]

There's a variety of new greetings and service refusal lines for all service classes, with extra weather-specific lines for travel services.

The greetings are given low priority to avoid overriding unique or quest-related dialogue. 

[b][size=4]Compatibility[/size][/b]

This mod will automatically cover NPCs added by mods, as long as they were assigned one of the vanilla service classes.

A Tamriel_Data add-on is available, to cover the new service classes created for Tamriel Rebuilt and the Project Tamriel province mods (bakers, jewelers, potters, etc.).  Confirmed to be compatible with the Poison Song update! Unfortunately I'm unable to add support for the custom weather types these mods introduce (sand and tropical storms).

Aside from adding new classes, mods can also add services to NPCs with a non-service class. This is sometimes done to bypass skooma trading restrictions. As a result, service refusal coverage for modded NPCs may not always be perfect.

[b][size=4]Recommended mods[/size][/b]

Sorry Too Stormy was designed to work great alongside [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56629]Sorry We're Closed[/url], the nighttime variant of this mod. Load order of the two mods doesn't matter. 

Weather mods like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60258]Expanding Blight (OpenMW)[/url],[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47904] Creeping Blight [/url]or [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52354]Solthas Blight Weather Pack[/url] (Weather Rebalance module) make it possible for ash and blight storms to occur in more regions.

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48610]Improved Inns Expanded[/url] will make it easier to find a place to rest for a while, until the weather clears up.

Survival mods like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/49057]Ashfall[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57526]Sun's Dusk[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56480]Devilish Needs[/url] make weather conditions have more impact on your character.  

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47253]Djangos Dialogue[/url] adds lots of new dialogue, some of it based on weather and time of day. My greetings will take priority over some of Djangos' greetings, to keep them consistent with the service refusal.

name: Under Construction
author: Necrolesian
description: Construction materials and scaffolding are now visible at the Great House strongholds during construction of the later stages.
usage_notes:
[center][u][b]Under Construction [/b][/u][/center]
 
[b]Summary [/b]
 
With this mod, construction materials and scaffolding will be visible at the Great House strongholds during construction of the later stages.
 
[b]Description [/b]
 
It's commonly understood that the Great House strongholds have three stages, but they actually have six phases. In addition to the three main stages, there are also three intermediate phases during which various portions of the stronghold are under construction. Bethesda implemented the first intermediate phase (where the first stage of the stronghold is under construction), but did not fully implement the other two (where the second and third stages are in progress).
 
The developers went to the trouble of creating the required objects (scaffolding, wood planks, buckets, and so on) and placing them in the world, as well as assigning them scripts to ensure they'll only be visible during the appropriate construction phases. However, they just never actually set the relevant global variable to the proper values to implement these later intermediate phases.
 
When construction first begins on your stronghold, the main building is inaccessible, and you'll see various construction materials nearby. But, in the vanilla game, due to Bethesda's partial implementation, there are no such intermediate phases later on. When construction of the second stage of the stronghold begins, there are no changes at the stronghold at all; when construction is complete, the new buildings pop into existence fully built. The same thing happens with the third stage.
 
This mod finishes the job that Bethesda started by implementing the last two intermediate phases. Now, when construction of the second or third stage of your stronghold begins, you can visit the stronghold and actually see the new buildings - inaccessible, for now - in progress, along with scaffolding and assorted construction materials lying about. The site foremen are also active during the intermediate phases.
 
After the requisite amount of time has passed, the under construction phase will be complete, the construction materials will be gone, and the new buildings will be accessible.
 
The mod also fixes a couple errors in the vanilla Raven Rock scripts (principally one that caused certain objects to be disabled when they shouldn't be), but does not otherwise touch Raven Rock.
 
[b]Installation [/b]
 
Use a mod management tool such as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45439]Wrye Mash[/url], or just copy the plugin to your Data Files directory and select it in the Morrowind Launcher.
 
[b]Compatibility [/b]
 
This mod edits the following vanilla scripts:
 
Strong_Build2_H
Strong_Build2_R
Strong_Build2_T
Strong_Build3_H
Strong_Build3_R
Strong_Build3_T
Strong3_Not
ColonyFactor3_D
Colony_E_Torch
 
It will be incompatible (without a patch at least) with any mod that touches the Strong_Build scripts. Stronghold overhauls should be okay, but any mod that changes the actual process of stronghold construction might touch the scripts.
 
I'm not aware of any other mods that edit the Strong3_Not script, but if one does, the conflict will be relatively minor - certain parts of Tel Uvirith that shouldn't be accessible until stage 3 is complete might be accessible during the under construction phase for stage 3.

Regarding the two Raven Rock (colony) scripts, if any other mod touches those scripts, it should come after this one in your load order.
 
The above script edits represent most of this mod's changes, although a couple manual adjustments to Tel Uvirith were necessary in order to prevent reaching certain areas before they're supposed to be accessible. The only actual cell edit is to the exterior cell Uvirith's Grave: placing two unopenable doors that will only be visible during the intermediate phase for stage 3. If you're using a mod that changes the exterior placement of Omavel's or Seleth's houses, this might result in a little weirdness. The other Tel Uvirith-related edits *shouldn't* result in conflicts, but I'm not 100% certain about that.
 
[b]Version History [/b]
 
Version 1.1 - 2021-10-05
   - Fixed a couple errors in the vanilla Raven Rock scripts, principally one that caused certain trees/rocks at the SE factor's estate location to be disabled when they shouldn't be.
   - Raven Rock is otherwise untouched.

Version 1.0 - 2021-09-29
   - Initial release.
 
[b]Contact [/b]
 
Feel free to contact me on the Nexus with any comments or suggestions. You can also find me on Discord as Necrolesian#9692.
 
[b]Usage [/b]
 
You can use this however you want.

name: Cavern Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Overhaul of almost all the caves on Vvardenfell utilizing Tamriel_Data.
usage_notes:
The overhauls this mod makes range from minor to medium. Fundamentally, these are still vanilla caves, preserving the thought put into them by Bethesda devs who designed them. 


All caves that are listed on [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Caves]this[/url] page were modified, with the exception of the Sixth House bases, the Corprusarium, Cavern of the Incarnate, Tukushapal and Urshilaku Burial Caverns. This mod also incorporates all the previous overhauls that I made and improves upon them, except for Sargon and Mount Kand, Cavern, which were remade from scratch for this mod.


Several things were done to improve the user experience:

1. Cluttering and detailing: no all-rockers, no rock spam that entirely covers the cave walls. I was going off of vanilla rock placements, and never strayed too far away from how it does certain things. Not a single cave exceeds 600 refs, so you can be sure that the cells this mod touches will not start lagging after you install this mod.
Cluttering was done where it made sense, whether it's beverages the bandits are drinking, or a set of Hortator cards/dices that they entertain themselves with.

2. Lighting: all new and modified vanilla light source placements are made to account for greenlighting and the 8-light-source-per-mesh Morrowind.exe limit (read more on greenlight [url=https://wiki.project-tamriel.com/wiki/Interior_Guidelines#Greenlight]here[/url]). That means that all of the 400 radius tikitorches were thrown out of the window, and replaced with 256/177/128 radius variants. While that helps with issues such a light leaks, some users may perceive the caves to be darker than before. Unfortunately, there is nothing that can be done with that, as this is how the vanilla engine handles lighting, and I wanted to give vanilla Morrowind.exe players a pleasant experience too alongside the per-pixel lighting users.
Aside from light source placements, all ambient and sunlight lighting values were standardized. Sunlight values are 10/10/10 for all cells, and ambient lighting is increased and given a color based on the cave type. For mold caves I went with a mix of blue/green, mud caves are red/green to give off a yellow-ish hue, lava caves are given a red hue, mage caves (which have at least a single crystal placed) are given a blue-ish hue, and daedra-related caverns such as Kora-Dur and Dubdilla (the uncharted caverns part) were given a red/blue mix. It should be noted that there are exceptions to these standards.

3. Floaters, bleeders, caspers misplaced/misaligned objects: I thoroughly checked for any of the aforementioned issues that were present in vanilla caves, and tried my best to fix them. There are probably hundreds of fixes made by this mod.

4. Pathgrids: redone for every single cell this mod touches. While I can't claim that I'm experienced in pathgridding and know all the tricks, I tested every single cave in Morrowind.exe and can confirm that enemies navigate properly in and out of combat. OpenMW users should has even less issues with enemy AI. This also brings fixes by itself, too, such as unconnected nodes/underwater nodes being deleted.


Compatibility: incompatible with all mods that overhaul the locations this mod touches. The only compatible mods are those that create a whole other shell in the same cell and place the player there, leaving the original dungeon intact. I don't know about any mods which may place new quest items in cells that may conflict with this mod's placements, so please report those and I'll make a patch for them if I can. Lighting mods (Necro's TLAD, di.Still.ed Lights) should generally be fine to place above my mod, as the WGHT records weren't touched. Although I'm aware that TLAD makes edits to some cells so please report those incompatibilities too.


Due to the sheer amount of work poured into this mod, expect bugs and glitches. Don't forget to report them too.


The screenshots on the mod page may not correspond to individual user experience. I use OpenMW with core shader replacements and post-processing shaders.


Mod cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes.

name: Minor Tukushapal Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Minor overhaul of the Tukushapal burial cavern.
usage_notes:
As stated, the changes this mod makes are minimal. It's probably hard to even call it an overhaul. Still, I consider it an improvement over the original. 


As usual in my refit series, I fixed all the floaters/bleeders I could find, eliminated all instances of greenlight, edited pathgrids and edited the "Tukushapal" cell lighting settings to be less grey. The biggest amount of work in this mod is probably deleting all the internal geometry that was hidden behind the rocks. The developer probably initially made the shell with velothi pieces, then added rocks everywhere and forgot to clean up afterwards. I don't think this will actually bring a performance improvement but it's still a worthy change imo.


Compatibility: should be compatible with pretty much anything. 


Cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes.

name: Mine Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Overhaul of all the mines on Vvardenfell utilizing Tamriel_Data.
usage_notes:
This mod does several notable things, aside from the usual bugfixing, lighting and pathgrid improvements I make in my refit series. 

1. Quarters for miners! Yes, finally, all the FUNCTIONING mines have miner quarters. Did you ever notice that the vanilla mines were lacking that? Personally, I haven't. I don't think a lot of people care enough. I mainly added them because PTR does so, and I want this mod to be up to the project's standard. 

2. Utilizing TD kwama assets in egg mines.
TD introduces several new cool looking kwama assets that help diversify the egg mines which previously only had kwama eggs to somehow distinct themselves from other mines/caves, and this mod spreads them across all the egg mines. The care I put into the placement of these assets is magnitudes better than my old egg mine mod, which I'll still leave up for anyone who wants to download it, but under no circumstances do I recommend doing so. 

3. Adding new egg miners.
In several vanilla egg mines you could see NPCs named "Egg Miner", which is quite weird for MW which usually properly names all NPCs except guards. I added new records with properly named Egg Miners and changed their loot tables to give them egg miner hooks (new TD asset), new faces/hair and partially dressed them in TD clothing. This is probably the most compatibility problematic change this mod does, since some mods may use the vanilla records for quests. Please report such compatibility issues and I'll see what I can do.

For other stuff this mod does, consult [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57827]Cavern Refit's[/url]﻿ page description which gives a more in-depth explanation on what else you can expect from this modification.



Compatibility: incompatible with any mod that overhauls mines. I edited WGHT records in certain cells which will create incompatibilities with mods such as TLAD or di.still.ed Lights, so please place them above my mod in your load order.


Due to the amount of work poured into this mod, expect bugs and glitches. Don't forget to report them too.

post-processing shaders.

name: Velothi Tower Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Overhaul of all velothi towers on Vvardenfell.
usage_notes:
This mod overhauls all Vvardenfell velothi towers including Arvs-Drelen. 


The original interiors suffered heavily from dev crunch, which resulted in them being stale and unrewarding to explore. The clutter in most of them was straight up copypasted from other towers, with the exception of Arvs-Drelen and Ald Redaynia, which are the only towers that stand out somehow. I tried to fix that. Note that the tower layouts have not been changed or expanded, but rather heavily modified. I also did not stray from vanilla design choices, so if you are looking for an OAAB-style overhaul, unfortunately this isn't that.


I fixed bloaders, bleeders, caspers, greenlighting and pathgrids along with modifying the cell lighting, bringing it closer to Tamriel Rebuilt's standards.


Compatibility: most likely incompatible with any other mod heavily editing velothi towers.


The screenshots on the mod page may not correspond to individual user experience. I use OpenMW with core shader replacements and post-processing shaders.


Mod cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes and other issues

name: Vanilla Morrowind Trees - Animated
author: Silrorj and MOP team
description: Gives wind animations to the vanilla trees of Morrowind, Tribunal and Bloodmoon, based on the Morrowind Optimization Patch meshes.
usage_notes:
This mod adds a gentle wind animation to the vanilla trees of Morrowind, Tribunal and Bloodmoon. Leaves sway softly while trunks stay still, so the landscape feels a bit more alive without changing the look of the original trees.


It covers the trees of the Ascadian Isles, the Grazelands, the West Gash, the Bitter Coast (leaves and hanging moss), Mournhold and Solstheim (including the snowy pines), as well as a few small bushes. Dead and leafless trees are left untouched.


The meshes are based on the Morrowind Optimization Patch, so you keep all of its fixes and optimizations. MOP is not required, but if you use it, load this mod after it. 

Tree replacers that use the same meshes will override this mod for those trees, depending on your load order.

The performance impact is minimal, since only a few extra parts per tree are animated.


Credits go to the MOP team for the Morrowind Optimization Patch meshes, and to Vurt, whose animated trees inspired this mod

name: Tamriel Data Trees - Animated
author: Silrorj and TD team
description: Gentle animated leaf sway for over 500 trees from Tamriel Data.
usage_notes:
Adds gentle, subtle leaf sway to over 400 trees from Tamriel Data, covering Tamriel Rebuilt, Project Cyrodiil, Skyrim Home of the Nords and the other projects using it.


The foliage of each tree sways softly on its own loop, while trunks and collision stay static. Tall, narrow trees such as poplars and cone spruces sway gently as a whole from their base. 

Geometry, UVs and textures are identical to the original. Bare trees, trees that are already animated in Tamriel Data and underwater kelp trees are left untouched. 

Performance cost should be minimal.
This mod also fixes the flickering leaves on the Cyrodiil poplar, which were caused by overlapping leaves in the original model.
You need the original mod: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44537]Tamriel Data[/url]
Install after it and let this mod overwrite the meshes.


[u][b]Credits[/b][/u]: the Tamriel Data team and all the artists who created those trees, and Vurt for the animation method used in his Animated Solstheim Trees.

name: More Indoril Indoril Settlements
author: Damius
description: Updates Akamora, Ammar, Nan Iban, and Enamor Dayn to the newer Indoril tileset.
usage_notes:
[u][b]Summary[/b][/u]

When Poison Song released with its new Indoril tileset for Roa Dyr and talk of removing all the Mournhold architecture I was expecting the older Sacred East era Indoril settlements to have been updated too. I found out those have been shelved for a future full rework and rewrite potentially a few years out so for now we have a very stark divide between old and new content. 

I'm not patient enough for that so I’m updating them myself to the new tileset while keeping as close as possible to the original layout and intent. Some details had to be rearranged, like windows or entrances to diagonal buildings that don't have equivalents in the new tileset. [i]Most [/i]of the interiors are one for one swaps to their nearest equivalent parts, but the manors of the quest/plot related noble families were all remade to be chapel-manors. 

I also trimmed down the mountains and rocks around Akamora significantly, my fps went up for 30ish to about 60. There was quite a few rocks that were outright buried in a way that the player could never see, and a fair few that were massive but only the barest top was exposed so nothing significant was lost with their removal. This has also spilled out to some cells surrounding Akamora but not as heavily.

Note that I’m using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59978]my Indoril retexture[/url] in the screenshots.

[b][u]Planned[/u][/b]

My current plan is to work down the settlements that have quests first, then any that are likely to be visible going to or looking from quest related areas, then clean up of the remaining monasteries, plantations, and farms after.

[s]Nan Iban[/s] - Complete
[s]Enamor Dayn[/s] - Complete
Dreynim Spa - Exterior complete, interiors in progress

Sailen -  Exterior rough draft started

author: RandomPal -  Wolli  -  R0
description: Adds concept art balconies to the game, in Balmora and Suran.
usage_notes:
[size=3]I was looking at some Morrowind's conept art when I stumbled upon this drawing.[/size]

[img]https://images.uesp.net/4/44/MW-concept-19.jpg[/img]﻿

[size=3]One detail that really cought my eye was the balcony/staircase model. I was surprised to discovered that there wasn't a single mod that tried to implement that type of model into the game.

[b]As of version 2.0 the model has been remade from scratch[/b] by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/1615721]Wolli[/url]﻿, one of the best and most prolific modders and asset creators in the MW community.
There aren't many instances in the game where these new balconies can be used and I tried to use them well. Not every balcony has been replaced because variety is also improtant and because the vanilla balcony models are actually really good and I'd say iconic at this point.
The mod [b]also includes simple scenic balconies[/b] as seen in concept art. I used the models provided [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/43729]here[/url]. 
Due to the way vanilla design philosophy works, there wasn't a single place in the entire game where it made sense to use them, so it's not surprising that there ins't a mod making use of them. I expanded and tweaked 3 interior cells and replaced the exterior buildings with double floor versions to put these models to good use.
I hope you enjoy the mod!

[b]Installation[/b]
The mod is fully modular.
00 Core folder has the assets
01 adds the new balconies to Balmora
02 to Suran (with a version available for people using White Suran by MD)

[b]Compatibility
[/b]Should be compatible with pretty much everything. 
My mods [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48675]Suran - The Pearl of the Ascadian Island [/url]and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48807]Balmora - Seat of Power of House Hlaalu[/url] already include the new balconies so you don't need this mod if you're using them.[/size]

name: Balmora Morag Tong Guildhall Redone
author: Markond
description: Changes the exterior of the Balmora Morag Tong guildhall, with a few small interior changes.
usage_notes:
[u][b]Summary[/b][/u]

I've seen a few big Balmora overhauls swap out the Balmora Morag Tong guildhall for the domed hlaalu hall from TR, but none that were standalone. So I made my own. Swaps the exterior, with a few changes to the interior to match the new shell.

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44537]TRData[/url]
[b]

There is a second lamp post left deliberately where it adds a new lantern to catch it,[b] [/b]and there is a deliberate change to four desks that tescmd/wrye bash cleaning reads as a mistake and attempts to fix. These are deliberate to maintain compatibility. If you find the desks are floating then you need to run it further below BCOM iun your load order, or you cleaned it and broke that part.

name: The Bard's Mini-Mods
author: Titus the Bard
description: A collection of my smaller mods that make very minor changes to the game.
usage_notes:
Some very minor changes to Morrowind that aim to increase immersion. Each of the changes can be downloaded as separate plugins.

[*]Recommended to be used with lhyacinth's [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58836]Make a Profit[/url]. Make sure to enable the contraband settings (disabled by default).[/*]

While this is a small issue, it can be noticeable when playing with mods that rely on region data for certain features.[/*]
